text: This work proposes a novel model to manipulate individual visual attributes of objects in a real scene, addressing the challenge of properties difficult to measure or represent as real-valued vectors. Our approach trains the model to manipulate a specific property in isolation by leveraging only "synthetic demonstrations" from simulations, such as nonphotorealistic 3D renders of a face with varied expression, without explicitly provided labels. Our results demonstrate that the model effectively preserves all other visual attributes of a real face, such as head orientation, despite these attributes not being labeled. We further quantify this preservation degree and analyze the impact of attribute distribution discrepancies using digit datasets, ultimately demonstrating robust performance in the more difficult setting of manipulating real human faces using nonphotorealistic 3D renders. This methodology holds significant implications for future research, offering broad applicability to manipulate shape, texture, lighting, and other complex visual properties that are difficult to measure or represent directly.

text: With the advancements made in deep learning, computer vision problems like object detection and segmentation have seen a great improvement in performance. However, in many real-world applications such as autonomous driving vehicles, the risk associated with incorrect predictions of objects is very high. Standard deep learning models for object detection such as YOLO models are often overconfident in their predictions and do not take into account the uncertainty in predictions on out-of-distribution data. In this work, we propose an efficient and effective approach to model uncertainty in object detection and segmentation tasks using Monte-Carlo DropBlock (MC-DropBlock) based inference. The proposed approach applies drop-block during training time and test time on the convolutional layer of the deep learning models such as YOLO. We show that this leads to a Bayesian convolutional neural network capable of capturing the epistemic uncertainty in the model. Additionally, we capture the aleatoric uncertainty using a Gaussian likelihood. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on modeling uncertainty in object detection and segmentation tasks using out-of-distribution experiments. Experimental results show that MC-DropBlock improves the generalization, calibration, and uncertainty modeling capabilities of YOLO models in object detection and segmentation.

text: Motivated by the significant impact of cache managers on computer system performance and the need for optimal strategies to maximize hit rates while minimizing storage, this study investigates reinforcement learning (RL) to guide general-purpose cache manager decisions. The approach involved designing three separate RL agents for distinct cache tasks, exploring both single multi-task and multi-agent architectures, and introducing a novel framework to simplify modeling computer systems problems as RL tasks; this framework abstracts delayed experiences observations and reward assignment in computer systems while providing a flexible way to scale to multiple agents. Simulation results using an established database benchmark system demonstrate that RL agents achieve higher cache hit rates and minimize required space more effectively than heuristic driven algorithms, while also adapting to a changing workload and dynamically adjusting their caching strategy accordingly. This research, the first to model cache manager decisions as a multi-task control problem, offers a generic model applicable to other types of caches, such as file system caches, suggesting new directions for intelligent, adaptive cache management.

text: 158-word abstract for the paper {file_name}: This paper addresses the motivation of enabling unsupervised detection and segmentation of objects in live scenes, defined as portions that move coherently. The approach partitions motion fields by minimizing mutual information, then uses segments to train deep neural networks (for static and dynamic models) jointly via a bootstrapping strategy for object modeling and extrapolation to unseen objects. Training uses motion, but inference works on static images/videos. As video volume grows, seen moving objects prime detection and regularize new object learning, enabling unsupervised continual learning. Results show that on six benchmark datasets, these models compare favorably to state-of-the-art methods in video object segmentation and salient object detection, even those using pixel-level supervision, despite requiring no manual annotation. The success of this unsupervised continual learning approach from motion has significant implications for future research, paving the way for scalable object understanding from vast unlabeled video corpora and the development of more adaptive, self-improving visual systems.

text: –Positional Encoding: Positional encoding is used in transformers to provide positional information, helping the model understand the relative positions of words in the input sequence, as they do not have an inherent notion of word order. This is critical because the self-attention mechanism, while powerful for capturing contextual relationships, processes all tokens simultaneously, effectively losing the sequential information inherent in ordered data. To compensate, positional encodings, often generated using fixed sinusoidal functions (as proposed in the original Transformer architecture) or learned embeddings, are superimposed onto the token embeddings before they are fed into the transformer layers. This augments the token representations with a unique signature indicating their position within the sequence, allowing the model to distinguish between identical tokens appearing at different locations and to capture dependencies that rely on word order. In the specific domain of smart contract vulnerability detection, preserving the precise sequence of operations, function calls, and variable accesses is paramount, as the order of code elements frequently dictates the presence and type of a security flaw. For instance, a reentrancy vulnerability is fundamentally defined by a specific sequence of an external call followed by a state modification, which positional encoding helps the language model recognize and differentiate from benign code patterns, thereby enabling more accurate multi-label classification of complex vulnerabilities like reentrancy, integer overflows, or unchecked external calls.

text: Trong quá trình đánh giá hiệu suất của mô hình phân loại, các kết quả dự đoán so với nhãn thực tế được phân chia thành bốn trường hợp cơ bản: **True Positive (TP)** xảy ra khi một đối tượng thực tế thuộc lớp Positive được mô hình phân loại chính xác vào lớp Positive; **True Negative (TN)** xảy ra khi một đối tượng thực tế thuộc lớp Negative được mô hình phân loại chính xác vào lớp Negative; **False Positive (FP)** xảy ra khi một đối tượng thực tế thuộc lớp Negative bị mô hình phân loại nhầm thành lớp Positive, còn được biết đến là Lỗi loại I (Type I Error); và **False Negative (FN)** xảy ra khi một đối tượng thực tế thuộc lớp Positive bị mô hình phân loại nhầm thành lớp Negative, còn được biết đến là Lỗi loại II (Type II Error). Các trường hợp này đóng vai trò nền tảng và thường được tổng hợp một cách trực quan trong ma trận hỗn loạn (confusion matrix) nhằm cung cấp cái nhìn toàn diện về hiệu suất của mô hình.

text: With its extensibility, Postgres allows users to define custom data types, functions, and stored procedures, enabling tailored solutions to specific requirements; this capability is particularly vital for a complex ERP system like Odoo, which often requires highly specific data schemas to represent diverse business processes, such as unique ticket statuses, custom fields for incident reporting, or specialized user roles within a helpdesk environment, with support for procedural languages like PL/pgSQL further empowering developers to implement intricate business logic directly within the database for optimized performance in operations like complex report generation or automated ticket routing. Furthermore, its architecture supports advanced features like Foreign Data Wrappers (FDW), facilitating seamless integration with external data sources—a common requirement for comprehensive helpdesk solutions needing to pull information from CRM or inventory systems. It provides built-in support for concurrency control, enabling multiple users to access and modify data concurrently; this is achieved through its robust Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) mechanism, which allows simultaneous read and write operations without imposing read locks, ensuring data consistency and high availability by preventing common database contention issues, and guaranteeing that multiple users can access and modify data concurrently without experiencing deadlocks or inconsistent reads, crucial for maintaining the responsiveness and reliability of a high-traffic support system for the Odoo-based helpdesk.

text: Trong quá trình thực hiện các thí nghiệm với các tỷ lệ khác nhau giữa ảnh GAN và ảnh thật, em tiến hành xây dựng các tập dữ liệu pha trộn theo các tỷ lệ 10:90, 30:70, 50:50, 70:30 và 90:10, trong đó tỷ lệ đầu tiên thể hiện phần trăm ảnh GAN và tỷ lệ còn lại là ảnh thật. Đối với mỗi tập dữ liệu, mô hình nhận diện chữ viết được huấn luyện từ đầu với cùng một cấu hình kiến trúc và các siêu tham số giống nhau để đảm bảo tính nhất quán trong quá trình so sánh. Các chỉ số đánh giá được sử dụng bao gồm độ chính xác (accuracy), độ nhạy (recall), độ đặc hiệu (specificity) và điểm F1 (F1-score) nhằm phản ánh toàn diện hiệu suất của mô hình. Kết quả thực nghiệm cho thấy khi tỷ lệ ảnh GAN thấp (10% GAN và 90% ảnh thật), độ chính xác của mô hình giảm không đáng kể so với khi chỉ sử dụng ảnh thật. Tuy nhiên, khi tăng dần tỷ lệ ảnh GAN, đặc biệt ở mức 50% trở lên, hiệu suất của mô hình bắt đầu suy giảm rõ rệt trên cả bốn chỉ số đánh giá. Điều này cho thấy các ảnh sinh tổng hợp từ GAN mặc dù có thể bổ sung về mặt số lượng dữ liệu, nhưng chất lượng của chúng vẫn chưa đạt được sự tương đồng hoàn toàn với ảnh thật, dẫn đến việc mô hình bị nhiễu thông tin và giảm khả năng tổng quát hóa. Đáng chú ý, ở tỷ lệ 70% hoặc 90% ảnh GAN, mô hình không chỉ giảm độ chính xác mà còn xuất hiện hiện tượng overfitting nhẹ, thể hiện ở sự chênh lệch lớn giữa độ chính xác trên tập huấn luyện và tập kiểm tra. Điều này có thể lý giải do ảnh GAN có xu hướng tạo ra các mẫu dữ liệu mới không đủ đa dạng hoặc không phản ánh đúng các đặc trưng tự nhiên của dữ liệu chữ viết tay thực tế. Bên cạnh đó, khi tiến hành phân tích sâu hơn về từng lớp từ vựng, kết quả cho thấy ảnh hưởng tiêu cực của ảnh GAN không đồng đều giữa các lớp. Một số ký tự phức tạp hoặc ít xuất hiện trong tập dữ liệu gốc bị mô hình nhận diện sai nhiều hơn khi bổ sung ảnh GAN, trong khi các ký tự phổ biến ít bị ảnh hưởng. Điều này gợi mở rằng việc sinh ảnh GAN hiện tại chưa khai thác tốt các đặc trưng tinh vi của từng lớp dữ liệu, đặc biệt là đối với những lớp có tần suất xuất hiện thấp. Ngoài ra, để kiểm tra khả năng ứng dụng thực tế, em đã tiến hành kiểm thử mô hình trên một tập dữ liệu hoàn toàn mới gồm các mẫu chữ viết tay chưa từng xuất hiện trong quá trình huấn luyện. Kết quả tiếp tục cho thấy mô hình được huấn luyện với tỷ lệ ảnh GAN cao có độ chính xác giảm mạnh, trong khi mô hình chủ yếu sử dụng ảnh thật hoặc pha trộn tỷ lệ nhỏ ảnh GAN giữ được độ ổn định tốt hơn. Từ các kết quả thực nghiệm trên, có thể rút ra rằng phương pháp bổ sung dữ liệu bằng ảnh sinh từ GAN chỉ thực sự hiệu quả khi tỷ lệ ảnh GAN được kiểm soát ở mức thấp và cần kết hợp với các kỹ thuật tăng cường dữ liệu truyền thống để đảm bảo chất lượng và tính đa dạng của tập huấn luyện. Đồng thời, việc cải tiến các mô hình GAN theo hướng sinh ảnh có chất lượng cao hơn, phản ánh sát thực tế hơn sẽ là hướng nghiên cứu cần thiết để nâng cao hiệu quả cho các bài toán nhận diện chữ viết tay trong tương lai.

Đóng góp của nghiên cứu hiện tại là đề xuất một giải pháp cụ thể để xử lý tình huống suy giảm tầm nhìn do ánh sáng mạnh, qua đó tăng cường an toàn khi tham gia giao thông.

Existing deep reinforcement learning (RL) for session-based recommendations typically necessitates costly online interactions or relies on potentially biased user-behavior models. This work addresses the challenge of learning recommendation policies purely from offline historical interaction logs, without access to real-world data or user models. We propose BCD4Rec: Batch-Constrained Distributional RL for Session-based Recommendations, which leverages advancements in batch (offline) RL and distributional RL to learn from offline logs while accounting for inherently stochastic user rewards due to latent interests. Our results demonstrate that BCD4Rec significantly outperforms behavior policies and strong RL/non-RL baselines in the batch setting, measured by Click Through Rates and Buy Rates. Furthermore, BCD4Rec effectively recommends items from correct latent categories despite large action spaces and mitigates popularity bias prevalent in offline logs, offering a robust offline RL solution.

text: Future wireless networks, driven by the demanding requirements of mobile edge computing (MEC) applications and functions, necessitate the high-capacity and dense deployment of MEC hosts. However, operating such high-capacity MEC hosts significantly increases energy consumption, prompting the exploration of self-powered base station (BS) units. This paper investigates an effective energy dispatch mechanism for self-powered wireless networks with integrated edge computing capabilities. This research first formulates a two-stage linear stochastic programming problem to minimize the total system energy consumption cost while fulfilling energy demand. Subsequently, a semi-distributed data-driven solution, employing a novel multi-agent meta-reinforcement learning (MAMRL) framework, is proposed to address this problem. Within this framework, each BS functions as a local agent, exploring Markovian behavior for energy consumption and generation, and transmitting time-varying features to a meta-agent. The meta-agent then optimizes energy dispatch decisions by incorporating observations from local agents and its own state information, while each BS agent concurrently estimates its energy dispatch policy using parameters learned from the meta-agent. The proposed MAMRL framework is evaluated across deterministic, asymmetric, and stochastic environments, assessing its performance in terms of non-renewable energy usage, energy cost, and prediction accuracy. Experimental results indicate that the MAMRL model significantly reduces non-renewable energy usage by up to 11% and energy costs by 22.4%, achieving 95.8% prediction accuracy when compared against existing baseline methods.

text:
The opioid crisis remains a critical public health challenge, necessitating accurate and timely forecasting of overdose incidents to inform intervention strategies. This paper introduces CASTNet (Community-Attentive Spatio-Temporal Networks), a novel deep learning framework designed to predict opioid overdose trends by leveraging spatio-temporal data with a focus on community-specific dynamics. CASTNet integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) to model spatial dependencies and temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) to capture temporal patterns, while incorporating an attention mechanism to prioritize community-level features that influence overdose risks. The model is trained and evaluated on a comprehensive dataset comprising overdose incidents, demographic data, and environmental factors across multiple regions. Experimental results demonstrate that CASTNet outperforms existing methods in forecasting accuracy, achieving a 15% improvement in mean absolute error (MAE) compared to state-of-the-art approaches. The framework’s ability to identify high-risk communities and predict overdose trends with high precision highlights its potential for enabling targeted public health interventions. CASTNet represents a significant advancement in spatio-temporal forecasting, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for addressing the opioid crisis and similar public health challenges.  

**Keywords**: opioid overdose forecasting, spatio-temporal networks, graph neural networks, attention mechanisms, public health, deep learning.

Trong khuôn khổ phát triển hệ thống, việc xác định các `use case` đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc mô tả tương tác giữa người dùng và hệ thống, từ đó định hình các chức năng chính. Hệ thống được đề xuất bao gồm các `use case` cốt lõi, được tổng hợp chi tiết trong `Bảng 2.2: Danh sách các use case`, bao gồm: `UC01: Thêm tài khoản người dùng, quản trị viên`; `UC02: Quản lý danh mục`; `UC03: Quản lý các loại sách`; `UC04: Quản lý đơn mượn, trả sách`; và `UC05: Quản lý gói sách`.

Đi sâu vào đặc tả, `use case` `UC01: Thêm tài khoản người dùng, quản trị viên` (mục 2.3.1) được thiết kế để người quản trị hệ thống có toàn quyền khởi tạo và quản lý các tài khoản. Cụ thể, chức năng này cho phép người quản trị thêm mới tài khoản cho cả đối tượng quản trị viên khác và người dùng cuối, đồng thời thực hiện việc phân quyền chi tiết, gán các quyền hạn truy cập và thao tác tương ứng cho từng tài khoản. Nghiên cứu hiện tại đóng góp vào việc cụ thể hóa các yêu cầu chức năng thông qua một bộ `use case` rõ ràng, đặc biệt là `UC01`, nhằm nâng cao khả năng quản trị và bảo mật cho hệ thống, một yếu tố thường được nhấn mạnh trong các công trình về phát triển phần mềm an toàn (ví dụ, McGraw, 2006). `Bảng 2.2` cung cấp một cái nhìn tổng quan, trong khi đặc tả chi tiết của từng `use case` như `UC01` làm rõ hơn các tương tác cụ thể.

The main idea of this passage is the secure transmission of information between parties using JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). The text discusses JWTs' capability for signing with public/private key pairs, ensuring sender authenticity and content integrity, since the signature is derived from both the header and the payload.

JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) represent a robust method for securely transmitting data between parties. By employing signing mechanisms, such as public/private key pairs, JWTs provide assurance regarding the authenticity of the sender's identity. This cryptographic signing ensures that the originators of the messages are indeed who they claim to be. Moreover, since the signature is generated based on the header and payload contents, it allows recipients to verify that the transmitted information has not been altered or tampered with during transit. As a result, JWTs maintain both the integrity and authenticity of data exchange, contributing significantly to secure information sharing protocols.

text:
Tiny object detection remains a significant challenge in computer vision due to the limited spatial information and low resolution of such objects. This paper investigates the role of the Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) in improving detection accuracy for tiny objects by analyzing the effective fusion factor within the FPN architecture. We propose a novel approach to optimize feature fusion by dynamically adjusting the contribution of different pyramid levels based on object scale and contextual information. Our method leverages a lightweight attention mechanism to enhance the fusion process, ensuring that fine-grained details from lower-level features are effectively integrated with semantic-rich higher-level features. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including COCO and Pascal VOC, demonstrate that our approach achieves a significant improvement in detection performance for tiny objects, outperforming existing FPN-based methods by 5-7% in mean Average Precision (mAP). The results highlight the importance of adaptive feature fusion in addressing the challenges of tiny object detection. This work contributes to advancing object detection systems, particularly in applications such as surveillance, medical imaging, and autonomous driving, where detecting small objects is critical.  

**Keywords**: Tiny object detection, Feature Pyramid Network (FPN), feature fusion, attention mechanism, computer vision, object detection.

text: In FedAvg, the central server aggregates the model parameters received from participating nodes by averaging them. However, FedAvg suffers from a slower convergence rate and lower accuracy, particularly when dealing with non-IID data distributed across nodes. It is important to note that the contributions of participating nodes to the training process are often unequal, making the uniform averaging of local model parameters potentially suboptimal. To address FedAvg’s convergence limitations, Federated Adaptive Weighting (FedAdp) was proposed. FedAdp mitigates this issue by assigning unique weights to each participating node for updating the global model, based on their contributions in each communication round. These contributions are initially assessed by measuring the angle between the local and global gradient vectors, followed by a non-ar mapping function to quantify the weights. FedAdp demonstrates superior performance over FedAvg, especially with non-IID data. Experimental results reveal that FL training with FedAdp reduces the number of communication rounds required to achieve 95% test accuracy on the MNIST dataset by up to 54.1% compared to FedAvg. Similarly, FedAdp decreases the communication rounds needed to reach 80% test accuracy on the FashionMNIST dataset by up to 45.4% relative to FedAvg. Nevertheless, FedAdp has a limitation: the global gradient may not always align with the expected direction, as some participating nodes may lack data representing all labels, causing local gradients to diverge from the intended path.

text: In this paper we propose a novel image representation called face X-ray for detecting forgery in face images. The face X-ray of an input face image is a greyscale image that reveals whether the input image can be decomposed into the blending of two images from different sources. It does so by showing the blending boundary for a forged image and the absence of blending for a real image. We observe that most existing face manipulation methods share a common step: blending the altered face into an existing background image. For this reason, face X-ray provides an effective way for detecting forgery generated by most existing face manipulation algorithms. Face X-ray is general in the sense that it only assumes the existence of a blending step and does not rely on any knowledge of the artifacts associated with a specific face manipulation technique. Indeed, the algorithm for computing face X-ray can be trained without fake images generated by any of the state-of-the-art face manipulation methods. Extensive experiments show that face X-ray remains effective when applied to forgery generated by unseen face manipulation techniques, while most existing face forgery detection or deepfake detection algorithms experience a significant performance drop.

text: The main idea of the paragraph is to describe the process by which PostgreSQL handles a query from a client application, detailing the roles of the query parser, optimizer, and executor in transforming a client query into an executable plan. When a client application submits a query to PostgreSQL, the system initially processes the query through the query parser, which is responsible for parsing and analyzing the input. Following this, the parsed query is forwarded to the query optimizer, which constructs an optimal execution plan by considering available indexes, statistical data, and estimated costs. Finally, the query executor carries out this plan, thereby completing the query processing workflow. This multi-stage process ensures that queries are executed efficiently, leveraging PostgreSQL’s robust query optimization mechanisms as discussed in related works such as Stonebraker and Kemnitz (1991) and Momjian (2001). The approach outlined here is fundamental to the effectiveness and performance of PostgreSQL in enterprise resource planning applications, as illustrated in the development and implementation of the helpdesk website using OdooErp.

text:
Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution images from low-resolution counterparts, a task critical for applications in medical imaging, surveillance, and multimedia. Traditional SISR methods often rely on supervised learning with paired datasets, which are difficult to obtain and may not generalize well to real-world degradation scenarios. This paper introduces an unsupervised degradation learning framework for SISR, eliminating the need for paired training data. Our approach leverages a novel degradation model that learns the underlying degradation process directly from unpaired low- and high-resolution images. By combining a generative adversarial network (GAN) with a self-supervised learning mechanism, the proposed method effectively captures complex degradation patterns, such as noise, blur, and compression artifacts. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing unsupervised SISR methods in terms of both visual quality and quantitative metrics, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. The proposed method also shows robustness to diverse degradation types, making it highly applicable to real-world scenarios. This work advances the field of SISR by providing a practical and scalable solution for unsupervised degradation learning, with potential applications in image restoration and enhancement.  

**Keywords**: Single Image Super-Resolution, Unsupervised Learning, Degradation Model, Generative Adversarial Network, Image Restoration.

text: This paper introduces an online initialization method for bootstrapping optimization-based monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), addressing the simultaneous online calibration of spatial and temporal offsets between the camera and IMU, alongside the estimation of initial metric scale, velocity, gravity, gyroscope bias, and accelerometer bias during initialization. The proposed approach incorporates two short-term motion interpolation algorithms to mitigate time offset impacts on camera and IMU pose estimation, and applies a three-step incremental parameter estimation process: (1) extrinsic rotation, gyroscope bias, and time offset estimation via rotation difference minimization; (2) approximate estimation of metric scale, gravity, and extrinsic translation using compensated camera poses while neglecting accelerometer bias; and (3) parameter refinement considering accelerometer bias and gravitational magnitude. To further enhance system state optimization, a nonlinear optimization algorithm that accounts for time offset is used for both global and local optimization. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate accurate estimation of initial values, extrinsic parameters, and sensor poses using the proposed method. (172 words)

Việc định giá bất động sản thường chỉ dựa trên khoảng vài chục thuộc tính, và mối quan hệ giữa giá bất động sản với các thuộc tính này được nhận thấy là phi tuyến tính (Król, 2015), do đó chúng tôi buộc phải sử dụng một mô hình phi tuyến. Mô-đun này không chỉ đảm bảo tính hợp lệ của định dạng mà còn thực hiện chuẩn hóa, ví dụ như xử lý các biến thể chồng chéo, các khoảng trống (gaps) hoặc các sự kiện cấu trúc lớn, để đảm bảo dữ liệu biến thể được biểu diễn một cách nhất quán cho các bước phân tích tiếp theo. Những thách thức chính ở đây bao gồm việc thiết kế các biểu thức chính quy (regular expressions) hoặc bộ phân tích ngữ cảnh (context-sensitive parsers) đủ linh hoạt để đối phó với sự đa dạng của các trường hợp `hgvsg_nput` có thể phát sinh từ các nguồn dữ liệu khác nhau, đồng thời duy trì hiệu suất cao. Hơn nữa, việc tích hợp các quy tắc kiểm tra tính toàn vẹn dữ liệu và cơ chế báo lỗi chi tiết là cần thiết để cảnh báo người dùng về các định dạng không hợp lệ hoặc các biến thể không thể diễn giải, từ đó nâng cao độ tin cậy của toàn bộ hệ thống. Song song với việc xử lý `hgvsg_nput`, tham số `refGenome` đóng vai trò tối quan trọng trong việc xác định bối cảnh bộ gen mà trình tự biến thể được ánh xạ tới. Sự lựa chọn giữa GRCh37 (còn được gọi là hg19) và GRCh38 (hg38) không chỉ đơn thuần là vấn đề phiên bản mà còn là một quyết định kỹ thuật sâu sắc, ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến tính chính xác của mọi phân tích. GRCh38 đại diện cho một bản nâng cấp đáng kể so với GRCh37, bao gồm các cải tiến về tính liên tục của trình tự (sequence continuity), bổ sung các vùng centromere và telomere, cùng với việc sửa đổi các trình tự thay thế (alternative contigs) và vá lỗi (patches) giúp giải quyết các vấn đề về độ bao phủ và sự sai lệch trong các vùng bộ gen phức tạp. Sai sót trong việc xác định `refGenome` có thể dẫn đến các lỗi nghiêm trọng như việc ánh xạ biến thể vào vị trí sai lệch, sai lầm trong việc truy vấn các cơ sở dữ liệu công cộng như dbSNP, ClinVar (vốn có thể được chú thích theo một phiên bản bộ gen cụ thể), hoặc lỗi trong việc dự đoán chức năng biến thể sử dụng các công cụ như SIFT hoặc PolyPhen. Để đảm bảo tính nhất quán và khả năng tái lập của kết quả, hệ thống của chúng tôi yêu cầu người dùng khai báo rõ ràng phiên bản `refGenome` và thực hiện kiểm tra chéo với bất kỳ nguồn dữ liệu tham chiếu bên ngoài nào. Trong trường hợp cần thiết, một mô-đun nâng cao có thể được phát triển để thực hiện "lift-over" tự động hoặc bán tự động, chuyển đổi tọa độ biến thể giữa các phiên bản bộ gen khác nhau, mặc dù quá trình này không phải lúc nào cũng hoàn hảo và có thể yêu cầu sự giám sát thủ công đối với các vùng bộ gen phức tạp. text: Corporate credit rating reflects the level of corporate credit and plays a crucial role in modern financial risk control. But real-world credit rating data usually shows long-tail distributions, which means heavy class imbalanced problem challenging the corporate credit rating system greatly. To tackle that, inspried by the recent advances of pre-train techniques in self-supervised representation learning, we propose a novel framework named Contrastive Pre-training for Corporate Credit Rating (CP4CCR), which utilizes the self-surpervision for getting over class imbalance. Specifically, we propose to, in the first phase, exert constrastive self-superivised pre-training without label information, which want to learn a better class-agnostic initialization. During this phase, two self-supervised task are developed within CP4CCR: (i) Feature Masking (FM) and (ii) Feature Swapping(FS). In the second phase, we can train any standard corporate redit rating model initialized by the pre-trained network. Extensive experiments conducted on the Chinese public-listed corporate rating dataset, prove that CP4CCR can improve the performance of standard corporate credit rating models, especially for class with few samples.

text: In recent years, significant channel morphology changes have been observed in most major rivers in Vietnam, including the Red River, Ma River, and Ca River. This phenomenon has led to considerable challenges in the management and operation of riparian irrigation systems, particularly culverts and pumping stations, during critical water supply periods. Although inter-reservoir operation procedures are established for various river basins, only the Red River basin currently possesses specific regulations regarding control points for minimum water levels and flows, which serve as a foundational basis for managers and operational units to develop production plans and manage the operation of water infrastructure. Conversely, other river basins, such as the Ca River basin, merely stipulate minimum discharge flows from irrigation and hydropower reservoirs, lacking defined downstream control points. text: Image interpolation, often referred to as image morphing, involves creating a visual transformation between two or more input images. For such transitions to be aesthetically pleasing, they should ideally be smooth, introduce the least necessary change, and appear realistic by avoiding unnatural artifacts throughout the sequence. The passage discusses the evolution and implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) since Alan Turing's foundational question, "Can machines think?", in 1950. It explains AI's objective to enable machines to make decisions independently, simulating human intelligence. Since Alan Turing first posed the question, "Can machines think?" in 1950, the quest to develop Artificial Intelligence (AI) has captivated scientific interest. AI aims to endow machines with the capability to make autonomous decisions, effectively mimicking human intelligence. This extends beyond mere programming, such as instructing a computer to follow traffic signals, to encompass learning behaviors akin to human emotions, such as road rage. AI is a vast domain within computer science, categorized into various sub-fields, as depicted in Figure 2.22. One prominent sub-field is Machine Learning (ML), which involves the study of computer algorithms capable of automatic improvement through experience and data utilization. ML is recognized as a subset of AI, where algorithms construct models from sample data, termed 'training data,' to make predictions or decisions regarding new data without explicit programming instructions. Enhancing the accuracy of these predictions typically involves augmenting training data, scaling data, tuning hyper-parameters, and applying dimensionality reduction techniques. Machine learning algorithms find applications across diverse domains, such as medicine, email filtering, speech recognition, and computer vision, particularly in scenarios where crafting conventional algorithms is challenging or impractical.

text: Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) traditionally presumes unrestricted access to both source and target domain data, with joint training to minimize the domain discrepancy. Nevertheless, such an assumption is often unrealistic in practical applications due to concerns over data privacy and the inefficiency of data transmission. This necessitates the development of methods that optimize network performance in the target domain without recourse to labeled source data. In pursuit of this objective within the context of object detection, this study introduces, for the first time, a source data-free domain adaptive object detection (SFOD) framework by reformulating the challenge as a learning problem with noisy labels. A commonly employed strategy involves leveraging a network pre-trained on the source domain to produce pseudo labels for optimizing the target domain. The principal challenge, however, lies in assessing the quality of these pseudo labels in the absence of ground-truth labels in the target domain. To address this, the paper proposes self-entropy descent (SED) as a metric for identifying a suitable confidence threshold for generating reliable pseudo labels, obviating the need for handcrafted labels. Despite this approach, perfectly clean labels remain unattainable, and comprehensive experimental analysis reveals that false negatives constitute the majority of noise in the generated labels. Targeted mining of false negatives is shown to enhance performance, and this process is facilitated through false negatives simulation via data augmentation, such as Mosaic. Extensive experiments across four representative adaptation tasks substantiate the ability of the proposed framework to readily achieve state-of-the-art performance. Furthermore, these findings prompt a reconsideration within the UDA community regarding the underutilization of labeled source data in current methodologies.

Trong bối cảnh ứng dụng di động, vấn đề này càng trở nên then chốt, bởi lẽ trải nghiệm người dùng (UX) là yếu tố quyết định đến mức độ chấp nhận, hài lòng và hiệu quả sử dụng của một ứng dụng (Nielsen, 1993; Shneiderman, 1998). Các công trình nghiên cứu trước đây đã phân tích sâu rộng tầm quan trọng của UX trong việc tối ưu hóa giao diện và tương tác (Garrett, 2011; Norman, 2013). Tuy nhiên, một khoảng trống vẫn tồn tại trong việc hiểu rõ cách thức những kỳ vọng chưa được thể hiện rõ ràng của người dùng có thể dẫn đến các vấn đề UX hoặc tạo ra sự mất hài lòng. Nghiên cứu hiện tại nhằm mục đích lấp đầy khoảng trống này bằng cách khảo sát mối liên hệ phức tạp giữa các kỳ vọng tiềm ẩn của người dùng và những thách thức về UX mà họ gặp phải khi sử dụng ứng dụng di động. Qua đó, công trình này kỳ vọng sẽ đóng góp vào việc phát triển các nguyên tắc thiết kế ứng dụng di động hiệu quả hơn, dựa trên sự thấu hiểu toàn diện về những mong đợi sâu sắc của người dùng.

text: Lemma 3 (Number of edges). Proof. Observe that for both x,y∈W(k−1, s), if there is an edge from vertex x= (x1, . . . , x k−1)to vertex y=y1, . . . , y k−1, then (x1, . . . , x k−1, yk−1)∈W(k, s). This establishes a mapping from each edge in the de Bruijn graph, where vertices correspond to words in `W(k-1, s)`, to a unique word in `W(k, s)`. Conversely, consider any word `z = (z1, . . . , zk)` from `W(k, s)`. By definition, its prefix `x = (z1, . . . , zk-1)` and its suffix `y = (z2, . . . , zk)` are both valid words within `W(k-1, s)`. An edge is therefore defined from `x` to `y` such that `(x1, . . . , x k−1, yk−1)` reconstructs `z`. Since every word in `W(k, s)` can be uniquely represented as an edge between two (k-1)-length words, and every such valid edge corresponds to a unique k-length word, a bijection exists between the set of edges in the de Bruijn graph whose vertices are drawn from `W(k-1, s)` and the set of words `W(k, s)`. Consequently, the total number of edges in this de Bruijn graph is precisely the cardinality of `W(k, s)`, thereby proving Lemma 3.

text: Our findings reveal that the use of Shapley value explanation provides a more detailed and accurate picture of feature importance in deep learning models than traditional methods. The hierarchical clustering approach allowed us to manage the complexity of the SVE computation effectively, providing a feasible way to analyze large datasets. In our experiments with the MNIST dataset, the SVE-derived feature importance correlated well with human perception, demonstrating the method's validity. When applied to fMRI data for ASD classification, SVE not only identified known biomarkers but also highlighted new potential biomarkers that were not previously recognized by standard Random Forest methods. This suggests that SVE can uncover deeper insights into the data, potentially leading to novel discoveries in ASD research. The comparison between SVE and Random Forest feature importance showed that while there is overlap in the most significant features, SVE offers a finer granularity of feature interaction, which could be crucial for understanding complex disorders like ASD. Our initial results on the ranked fMRI biomarkers using SVE on a deep learning classifier are promising, indicating that SVE can serve as a powerful tool in neuroimaging studies. Future work will involve exploring the application of SVE in other domains and refining the computational efficiency of the method, further broadening its utility in machine learning and medical imaging research.

text: Predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of industrial equipment is critical for optimizing maintenance schedules and reducing operational costs. This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating RUL by leveraging time series data and advanced machine learning techniques. We propose a novel approach based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) that utilizes time series embeddings to capture temporal dependencies and patterns in sensor data. Our method transforms raw sensor readings into low-dimensional embeddings, enabling efficient feature extraction and improving the model's ability to generalize across diverse datasets. The proposed model is evaluated on publicly available benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Key findings reveal that our approach achieves a significant reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) when compared to state-of-the-art techniques. The results highlight the potential of RNN-based time series embeddings for real-world applications in predictive maintenance. This research contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and interpretable framework for RUL prediction, which can be adapted to various industrial domains. Keywords: Remaining Useful Life (RUL), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), time series embeddings, predictive maintenance, machine learning.
label: deepseek-text

text:
Scene Graph Generation (SGG) is a critical task in computer vision, aiming to model the relationships between objects in an image as a structured graph. However, existing approaches often treat relation labels as flat categories, overlooking their inherent hierarchical structure, which can lead to suboptimal performance. This paper explores the hierarchical nature of relation labels in SGG and proposes a novel framework to leverage this hierarchy for improved relation prediction. Our approach introduces a hierarchical classification model that captures the dependencies and semantic relationships between different levels of relation labels, from coarse-grained to fine-grained. We evaluate our method on benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in relation prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art flat-label approaches. Additionally, our framework enhances interpretability by providing insights into the hierarchical structure of relations. The results highlight the importance of incorporating hierarchical information in SGG and open new avenues for research in structured visual understanding. Key contributions include a scalable hierarchical model, improved performance metrics, and a deeper understanding of relation label semantics. This work has implications for applications such as image captioning, visual question answering, and autonomous systems, where accurate and interpretable scene understanding is crucial.  

**Keywords**: Scene Graph Generation, Hierarchical Classification, Relation Prediction, Computer Vision, Structured Visual Understanding.

text:
Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown remarkable success in various domains, but its efficiency is often hindered by the need for extensive interaction with the environment. This paper addresses the challenge of experience reuse in RL by introducing a novel approach based on Policy Residual Representation (PRR). The objective is to enhance learning efficiency by leveraging past experiences to accelerate policy optimization in new tasks. We propose a framework that encodes the residual differences between policies, enabling the reuse of experiences across tasks with varying dynamics. Our method employs a deep neural network architecture to model these residuals, coupled with a dynamic experience replay mechanism that prioritizes relevant past experiences. Experimental results on benchmark environments demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces the sample complexity and improves convergence rates compared to traditional RL methods. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust performance in transfer learning scenarios, showcasing its ability to generalize across tasks with minimal additional training. The findings highlight the potential of PRR for advancing RL applications in real-world settings, where data efficiency and adaptability are critical. This work contributes a scalable and practical solution for experience reuse, paving the way for more efficient and versatile RL systems.  

**Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Experience Reuse, Policy Residual Representation, Transfer Learning, Sample Efficiency, Deep Neural Networks.
label: deepseek-text

text: Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) systems are crucial for enhancing the safety and efficiency of modern autonomous and assisted driving technologies. This paper describes an approach for efficiently detecting and recognizing traffic signs in real-time, specifically addressing challenges posed by varying weather, illumination, and visibility conditions through the application of transfer learning. The traffic sign detection problem is addressed using state-of-the-art multi-object detection systems, specifically Faster Recurrent Convolutional Neural Networks (F-RCNN) and Single Shot Multi- Box Detector (SSD) paired with various feature extractors (e.g., MobileNet v1 and Inception v2), alongside Tiny-YOLOv2. However, the primary focus of this paper is F-RCNN Inception v2 and Tiny YOLO v2, as these configurations demonstrated superior performance. These models were fine-tuned on the German Traffic Signs Detection Benchmark (GTSDB) dataset. Performance evaluation of these models was conducted on a host PC, a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+, and within the TASS PreScan simulation environment. The experimental results for all evaluated models are discussed in the conclusion section.

text: Property inference attacks aim to reveal statistical properties of a training set, yet are challenging to differentiate from the fundamental objective of statistical machine learning, which is to produce models that capture the underlying properties of a data distribution. Drawing on Yeom et al.'s membership inference framework, we introduce a formal and general definition of property inference attacks that characterizes attacks capable of distinguishing between possible training distributions, thereby generalizing previous approaches that focused on inferring the proportion of specific data types, such as the ratio of females in a dataset. We demonstrate that our definition encompasses existing property inference attacks and also facilitates new attacks, such as those that can uncover the average node degree or clustering coefficient within a training graph. Furthermore, our definition supports a theorem that relates the maximum possible accuracy of inference attacks distinguishing between distributions to the effective size of the dataset leaked by the model. To assess and quantify property inference risks, we perform a series of experiments across diverse distributions using both black-box and white-box attack methodologies. Our findings indicate that inexpensive attacks frequently match the effectiveness of more costly meta-classifier attacks and reveal unexpected asymmetries in attack success rates. Additionally, we extend the current state-of-the-art property inference attack methodology to convolutional neural networks and introduce techniques to identify model parameters that leak the most information, thereby substantially reducing the resource demands of meta-classifier attacks.

This modular design adheres to principles of loose coupling and high cohesion, making the user management layer easily pluggable into diverse applications beyond the scope of this specific news tracking system, thereby maximizing its long-term utility and reducing redundant development efforts for future projects requiring robust user authentication and authorization capabilities.

text: Obtaining dense 3D reconstrution with low computational cost is one of the important goals in the field of SLAM. In this paper we propose a dense 3D reconstruction framework from monocular multispectral video sequences using jointly semi-dense SLAM and Multispectral Photometric Stereo approaches. Starting from multispectral video, SALM (a) reconstructs a semi-dense 3D shape that will be densified;(b) recovers relative sparse depth map that is then fed as prioris into optimization-based multispectral photometric stereo for a more accurate dense surface normal recovery;(c)obtains camera pose that is subsequently used for conversion of view in the process of fusion where we combine the relative sparse point cloud with the dense surface normal using the automated cross-scale fusion method proposed in this paper to get a dense point cloud with subtle texture information. Experiments show that our method can effectively obtain denser 3D reconstructions.

text:
Graph representation learning (GRL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for analyzing complex relational data, with applications spanning social networks, biological systems, and recommendation engines. However, the practical deployment of GRL models faces significant challenges that hinder their effectiveness and scalability. This study aims to systematically quantify these challenges, focusing on issues such as data sparsity, scalability to large-scale graphs, and the interpretability of learned representations. We propose a comprehensive evaluation framework that assesses the performance of state-of-the-art GRL algorithms under varying conditions, including graph size, density, and noise levels. Our experiments reveal critical trade-offs between model accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness, highlighting the limitations of existing approaches. Furthermore, we identify key areas for improvement, such as the development of more efficient sampling techniques and the integration of domain-specific knowledge into GRL models. The findings provide actionable insights for researchers and practitioners, offering a roadmap for advancing the field of graph representation learning. This work contributes to the broader understanding of GRL by addressing its practical challenges and proposing directions for future research, ultimately enabling more effective and scalable applications in real-world scenarios.  

**Keywords**: graph representation learning, scalability, interpretability, data sparsity, evaluation framework, relational data.

text: This persistent gap below supervised performance, despite the advancements in self-learning, can be attributed to several inherent challenges within pseudo-labeling methodologies. For instance, the quality of pseudo-labels is often compromised by confirmation bias, where the model reinforces its own errors, particularly for classes that are difficult to distinguish or are underrepresented in the target domain, leading to the propagation of inaccuracies throughout the training process. While techniques such as those employed by DACS attempt to regularize the learning by mixing source and target data at the image or patch level, the primary reliance on softmax cross-entropy for supervising the student model with these pseudo-labels may not sufficiently enforce strong intra-class compactness and inter-class separability in the learned feature space, especially across the domain shift. Similarly, although adversarial training aims for global and class-wise feature alignment, it can sometimes struggle with training stability and may not explicitly optimize for the fine-grained feature consistency required for dense prediction tasks like semantic segmentation. These limitations underscore the need for mechanisms that can learn more discriminative and domain-robust features, perhaps by explicitly contrasting samples at multiple semantic levels to better handle noisy pseudo-labels and improve the model's ability to generalize from the source to the target domain, thereby offering a potential avenue to further enhance adaptation performance and bridge the gap to fully supervised methods.

The scarcity of high-quality annotated medical imaging data severely limits deep learning performance, despite its potential. While synthetic data addresses this, models often generalize poorly to real-world medical images. In this paper, {file_name} explores a novel approach leveraging cinematic rendering, which generates photorealistic medical images from CT data, to fine-tune deep learning networks. We propose fine-tuning synthetic data-driven networks using cinematically rendered CT data for monocular depth estimation in endoscopy. Our experiments demonstrate that networks fine-tuned with photorealistic cinematically rendered data adapt better and exhibit more robust performance on real medical images compared to non-fine-tuned models. Furthermore, these fine-tuned networks converge optimally with less training data, and diverse rendering conditions enhance model generalizability by preventing patient-specific learning. Our empirical evaluation shows a 56.87% and 27.49% reduction in error for rendered and real porcine colon endoscopy images, respectively. This work presents one of the first applications of cinematic rendering in deep learning, offering a promising solution to data scarcity and generalization challenges in medical AI.

text: Corporate credit rating, which gauges the creditworthiness of a corporation, is fundamental to contemporary financial risk management. However, real-world credit rating datasets typically exhibit long-tail distributions, leading to a significant class imbalance issue that severely impedes the efficacy of corporate credit rating systems. To address this challenge, drawing inspiration from recent advancements in pre-training techniques within self-supervised representation learning, we introduce a novel framework termed Contrastive Pre-training for Corporate Credit Rating (CP4CCR), which leverages self-supervision to mitigate class imbalance. Specifically, the initial phase involves applying contrastive self-supervised pre-training without relying on label information, aiming to acquire a superior class-agnostic initialization. Within this phase, CP4CCR incorporates two distinct self-supervised tasks: (i) Feature Masking (FM) and (ii) Feature Swapping (FS). Subsequently, in the second phase, any conventional corporate credit rating model can be trained using the weights initialized by the pre-trained network. Extensive experimentation performed on a Chinese public-listed corporate rating dataset demonstrates that CP4CCR significantly enhances the performance of standard corporate credit rating models, particularly for classes with limited samples.

text: This paragraph outlines the preprocessing techniques and model selection strategies employed in the Vietnamese multi-document summarization task. It emphasizes the use of a word segmentation model trained on Vietnamese datasets to prepare raw text for subsequent processing, the application of various Vietnamese tokenizers—including Phobert-large, ViT5-large, and a custom-trained Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer with a 34,000 vocabulary size on 5GB of preprocessed text—and the utilization of a Named Entity Recognition (NER) model trained on Vietnamese data to extract named entities, coupled with sentence selection guided by the Pyramid ROUGE score. These methodological choices aim to enhance the representation and extraction of relevant information for effective summarization. In this study, a word segmentation model trained on Vietnamese datasets was employed to preprocess raw textual data, thereby facilitating subsequent processing stages. Initially, the Phobert-large tokenizer was utilized to encode the dataset during preliminary experiments. Subsequently, experimentation extended to the ViT5-large tokenizer, alongside the development of a bespoke tokenizer trained via Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) with a vocabulary size of 34,000, derived from approximately 5GB of preprocessed Vietnamese text. Additionally, a Named Entity Recognition (NER) model, also trained on Vietnamese datasets, was applied to extract named entities, which informed the selection of sentences based on the Pyramid ROUGE score. This integrated approach leverages specialized Vietnamese language processing tools and evaluation metrics to improve the quality of multi-document summarization outputs.

4.3.2 Kiến trúc Frontend
Hình 4.13: Kiến trúc Frontend
Hình 4.13 mô tả kiến trúc chi tiết của phần Frontend. Các thành phần chính của kiến trúc frontend được tổ chức trong Đồ án Tốt nghiệp bao gồm: `containers`, `actions`, `reducers`, `store`, và `apps`. `Containers` là các thành phần tổng hợp, chịu trách nhiệm hiển thị giao diện cho ba trang chính: chi tiết lộ trình học, danh sách lộ trình học cần duyệt, và chi tiết duyệt lộ trình học. Mỗi `container` được cấu thành từ nhiều `component` con, tổ chức theo cấu trúc phân cấp dạng cây để tạo nên giao diện hoàn chỉnh của một trang. Ví dụ, `container Path Details` bao gồm hai `component` chính là `LeftSide` và `RightSide`. `Component LeftSide` hiển thị thông tin cơ bản của lộ trình học như tên, mô tả, thumbnail, trạng thái, cùng với hai nút chức năng để thay đổi thông tin cơ bản và nộp lộ trình học. `Component RightSide` hiển thị danh sách các khóa học trong lộ trình đó, kèm theo các nút chức năng như xóa khóa học, thay đổi thứ tự khóa học, xóa lộ trình học, tạo mới khóa học và chọn khóa học từ danh sách. Tương ứng với các tính năng này, `component LeftSide` chứa `component Modal Update Info`, và `component RightSide` chứa các `component` dạng `popup` như `New Course Form`, `Modal Delete`, và `Modal Choose Course` để hiển thị giao diện tương tác và thực thi các chức năng đó. Để dễ dàng truy xuất và tăng tính gọn gàng, dễ hiểu, dễ mở rộng của mã nguồn, các `actions` được đặt tên theo quy ước `đối tượng/hành động`, phân tách bởi dấu `/`. Ví dụ, `action '@@publishPath/OPEN_FILTER'` được sử dụng để lưu trữ thông tin về trạng thái đóng/mở của `popup` cho phép người dùng tùy chỉnh các cài đặt bộ lọc danh sách các lộ trình học đã nộp. Khi một `action` được gọi, nó sẽ kích hoạt các `reducers` tương ứng để thực hiện logic thay đổi trạng thái (state) dựa trên `action` và `payload` được truyền vào. Nếu nghiệp vụ yêu cầu tương tác với `apis` (ví dụ, các lời gọi đến backend), `reducers` sẽ gọi đến `api` tương ứng. Cuối cùng, `reducers` cập nhật trạng thái dựa trên dữ liệu truyền vào cũng như dữ liệu nhận được từ `apis` (nếu có) và chuyển những thay đổi này vào `store` để lưu trữ. Các giao diện trong `containers` sẽ tự động cập nhật ngay khi nhận được thông tin về sự thay đổi trạng thái từ `store`.

A comprehensive Helpdesk solution developed and deployed via OdooErp encompasses several critical features aimed at optimizing support workflows. The system enables straightforward data collection and facilitates the publication of databases online, thereby improving data accessibility. Centralized ticket management allows all customer inquiries to be consolidated within a single platform, while the omni-channel ticketing system ensures that queries from multiple sources are uniformly handled. Automated assignment rules can be configured to route tickets promptly to the appropriate department or agent, streamlining operations and reducing response times. The establishment of Service Level Agreements (SLAs) is instrumental in prioritizing urgent tickets, safeguarding against the risk of unanswered requests. Visual tools such as dashboards provide real-time access to essential metrics—including ticket volume, customer satisfaction ratings, and the frequency of ticket threads—which are crucial for operational oversight. Furthermore, the support team benefits from robust reporting capabilities that facilitate ongoing performance monitoring (see Table 3.5). Notably, comparable solutions such as Zoho incorporate AI-powered tools in their highest-tier offerings to further enhance support effectiveness, though these advanced features may present certain limitations as indicated in previous studies (Smith et al., 2022; Figure 1). The integration of these functionalities within OdooErp underscores its potential to streamline helpdesk management while enabling data-driven decision-making.

text: We study the task of conversational fashion image retrieval via multiturn natural language feedback. Most previous studies are based on single-turn settings. Existing models on multiturn conversational fashion image retrieval have limitations, such as employing traditional models, and leading to ineffective performance. We propose a novel framework that can effectively handle conversational fashion image retrieval with multiturn natural language feedback texts. One characteristic of the framework is that it searches for candidate images based on exploitation of the encoded reference image and feedback text information together with the conversation history. Furthermore, the image fashion attribute information is leveraged via a mutual attention strategy. Since there is no existing fashion dataset suitable for the multiturn setting of our task, we derive a large-scale multiturn fashion dataset via additional manual annotation efforts on an existing single-turn dataset. The experiments show that our proposed model significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

text: In a traditional convolutional layer, the learned filters stay fixed after training. In contrast, we introduce a new framework, the Dynamic Filter Network, where filters are generated dynamically conditioned on an input. We show that this architecture is a powerful one, with increased flexibility thanks to its adaptive nature, yet without an excessive increase in the number of model parameters. A wide variety of filtering operations can be learned this way, including local spatial transformations, but also others like selective (de)blurring or adaptive feature extraction. Moreover, multiple such layers can be combined, e.g. in a recurrent architecture. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the dynamic filter network on the tasks of video and stereo prediction, and reach state-of-the-art performance on the moving MNIST dataset with a much smaller model. By visualizing the learned filters, we illustrate that the network has picked up flow information by only looking at unlabelled training data. This suggests that the network can be used to pretrain networks for various supervised tasks in an unsupervised way, like optical flow and depth estimation.

text:
This paper introduces a novel approach to gradient boosting by incorporating piece-wise linear regression trees (PLRTs) as base learners. Traditional gradient boosting methods often rely on decision trees with constant values in leaf nodes, which can limit their ability to model complex, non-linear relationships. To address this limitation, we propose PLRTs, which utilize linear regression models in each leaf node, enabling more precise approximations of the underlying data patterns. The proposed method combines the strengths of gradient boosting and linear regression, offering improved predictive accuracy and interpretability.  

We evaluate the performance of our approach on several benchmark datasets, comparing it to conventional gradient boosting techniques and other state-of-the-art regression models. Experimental results demonstrate that PLRT-based gradient boosting consistently outperforms traditional methods, particularly in scenarios with intricate data structures. Additionally, we analyze the computational efficiency of the proposed method, showing that it maintains a reasonable trade-off between accuracy and training time.  

The key contribution of this work lies in the integration of piece-wise linear models within the gradient boosting framework, providing a flexible and powerful tool for regression tasks. This approach has significant implications for applications in domains such as finance, healthcare, and predictive analytics, where accurate and interpretable models are critical. Keywords: gradient boosting, piece-wise linear regression, decision trees, machine learning, regression models.

text: To address the crucial need for assessing generated image quality in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), this paper introduces a simple, non-interfering method applicable across GAN varieties. The approach centers on a Gaussian likelihood function, derived from the discriminator's embeddings of real images, to define two measures. These measures quantify the likelihood that generated image embeddings belong to the real image embedding distribution, yielding a fitness score. Empirical results on CIFAR-10 demonstrate a strong correlation between these measures and perceived image quality. Future research could leverage this for broader GAN evaluation, comparison, or to inform and guide GAN training processes.

Học có giám sát liên quan đến việc xây dựng mô hình dựa trên tập dữ liệu đã được gán nhãn, nơi mỗi ví dụ trong tập dữ liệu đã được gắn với một nhãn hoặc kết quả cụ thể. Ngược lại, học không giám sát không yêu cầu dữ liệu được gán nhãn, và mục tiêu là để khám phá cấu trúc hoặc mẫu ẩn trong dữ liệu. Trong bối cảnh của bài toán tự động trích xuất thông tin chữ viết từ hình ảnh, việc áp dụng các phương pháp học này có thể giúp cải thiện độ chính xác và hiệu quả của quá trình trích xuất. Đặc biệt, khi đánh giá hiệu suất của mô hình, các độ đo như Precision, Recall, và F1 score đóng vai trò quan trọng. Precision đo lường tỷ lệ dự đoán đúng trong số tất cả các dự đoán, Recall đo lường tỷ lệ dự đoán đúng trong số tất cả các trường hợp thực sự thuộc lớp dương tính, và F1 score là trung bình điều hòa của Precision và Recall, cung cấp một cái nhìn tổng quan về hiệu suất của mô hình. Trong bài toán phân loại nhị phân, việc phân biệt giữa lớp Positive (dương tính) và lớp Negative (âm tính) là rất quan trọng, và các định nghĩa như True Positive, False Negative, False Positive, và True Negative giúp đánh giá chính xác hiệu suất của mô hình trong việc phân loại các mẫu dữ liệu.

The introduced approach is compared with widely used local feature based methods (SURF, ORB) and the results indicate a clear improvement over the baseline. The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored the critical need for effective social distancing measures to mitigate infection risks. This paper presents *DeepSOCIAL*, a novel framework for real-time social distancing monitoring and infection risk assessment using advanced computer vision and deep learning techniques. The proposed system leverages YOLOv4 for accurate human detection and employs a customized deep neural network to estimate pairwise distances between individuals in crowded environments. Additionally, a risk assessment module integrates proximity data with epidemiological models to quantify potential infection risks. Evaluated on diverse datasets, *DeepSOCIAL* achieves high precision in distance estimation and demonstrates robust performance in varying lighting and crowd densities. Comparative analysis with existing methods highlights its superior accuracy and computational efficiency. The framework’s scalability and real-time capabilities make it a valuable tool for public health authorities and policymakers to enforce social distancing protocols and assess infection risks in public spaces. This research contributes to the growing body of work on AI-driven pandemic management, offering a practical solution for enhancing public safety during health crises.  

**Keywords**: social distancing, COVID-19, deep learning, computer vision, infection risk assessment, YOLOv4, real-time monitoring.

text: In image classification tasks, feature extraction presents a significant challenge. Specifically, intra-class variability complicates the design of robust feature extractors. Furthermore, traditional hand-crafted feature extractors often lack adaptability to novel or diverse data conditions. Recently, deep learning has garnered significant attention for its ability to automatically learn features directly from data. In this study, we propose the Multi-Subspace Neural Network (MSNN), which integrates a key component of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)—the receptive field—with the subspace concept. This association of subspace concepts with a deep network architecture represents a novel design, offering diverse perspectives on the data. Specifically, basis vectors, which are trained by an Adaptive Subspace Self-Organization Map (ASSOM) to span the subspace, serve as a transfer function to access axial components and define the receptive field, thereby enabling the extraction of fundamental data patterns without distorting the inherent topology in visual tasks. Moreover, the multiple-subspace strategy is implemented through parallel blocks, designed to process diverse real-world data and yield various interpretations, thereby enhancing robustness in addressing intra-class variability. To this end, handwritten digit (MNIST) and object image (COIL-20) datasets were employed to validate the proposed MSNN architecture in classification tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that MSNN is competitive with other state-of-the-art approaches.

This paper introduces a novel framework for zero-shot synthesis leveraging group-supervised learning, addressing the challenge of generating high-quality outputs without task-specific training data. Traditional synthesis methods often require extensive labeled datasets, limiting their applicability in scenarios where data is scarce or unavailable. To overcome this limitation, we propose a group-supervised learning approach that leverages shared patterns across diverse data groups to enable zero-shot generalization. Our method employs a hierarchical model architecture that learns group-level representations, enabling the synthesis of outputs for unseen tasks by transferring knowledge from related groups. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach across multiple domains, including image generation and text synthesis, achieving competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art supervised methods. The results highlight the model's ability to generalize to new tasks without explicit training, showcasing its potential for applications in low-resource environments. This work contributes to advancing zero-shot learning by introducing a scalable and efficient framework for synthesis tasks, with implications for AI-driven creativity, data augmentation, and cross-domain adaptation.

text: Point cloud completion involves deducing the entire geometry of 3D objects from incomplete data. Traditional methods typically rely on a global shape representation derived from the incomplete input to predict the complete point cloud. However, this global representation often leads to the loss of detailed structural information in the local regions of the incomplete point cloud. To tackle this issue, we introduce the Skip-Attention Network (SA-Net) for 3D point cloud completion. Our contributions are twofold. Firstly, we propose a skip-attention mechanism that effectively harnesses local structural details of incomplete point clouds during the inference of missing parts. This mechanism selectively transfers geometric information from local regions of incomplete point clouds to generate complete ones at various resolutions, offering an interpretable view of the completion process. Secondly, to fully leverage the geometric information encoded by the skip-attention mechanism across different resolutions, we present a novel structure-preserving decoder with hierarchical folding for generating complete shapes. This hierarchical folding progressively refines the local regions, maintaining the structure of the complete point cloud generated at higher levels, utilizing the skip-attentioned geometry at corresponding resolutions. Comprehensive experiments on the ShapeNet and KITTI datasets demonstrate that SA-Net surpasses existing state-of-the-art point cloud completion methods.

text: The BPE tokenization process operates according to a specific algorithm. Starting with a corpus and a predefined upper limit K for the number of merge operations, BPE tokenization identifies up to K merge operations and a set of subwords that together enable the construction of any word within the corpus. Initially, words are divided into sequences of characters. During each iteration, the algorithm tallies the frequency of each pair among the current types (initially characters), and then incorporates the merge operation for the most frequent pair into its set of operations. Subsequently, it updates the segmentation of all words based on the revised set of operations and proceeds to the following iteration.

text: We study defense strategies against reward poisoning attacks in reinforcement learning. As a threat model, we consider attacks that minimally alter rewards to make the attacker's target policy uniquely optimal under the poisoned rewards, with the optimality gap specified by an attack parameter. Our goal is to design agents that are robust against such attacks in terms of the worst-case utility w.r.t. the true, unpoisoned, rewards while computing their policies under the poisoned rewards. We propose an optimization framework for deriving optimal defense policies, both when the attack parameter is known and unknown. Moreover, we show that defense policies that are solutions to the proposed optimization problems have provable performance guarantees. In particular, we provide the following bounds with respect to the true, unpoisoned, rewards: a) lower bounds on the expected return of the defense policies, and b) upper bounds on how suboptimal these defense policies are compared to the attacker's target policy. We conclude the paper by illustrating the intuitions behind our formal results, and showing that the derived bounds are non-trivial.

Sự phát triển mạnh mẽ của kiến trúc Ứng dụng Trang đơn (SPA) và API-centric đã làm thay đổi cách thức mà các yêu cầu được khởi tạo và xử lý, từ đó tạo ra những thách thức mới trong việc triển khai các biện pháp phòng chống CSRF truyền thống. Tuy nhiên, việc quản lý mã thông báo này trong các ứng dụng SPA, nơi các yêu cầu được tạo động mà không có tải lại trang đầy đủ, có thể phức tạp, đòi hỏi cơ chế lấy và cập nhật mã thông báo hiệu quả từ phía client. Hơn nữa, nếu ứng dụng bị tấn công XSS, mã thông báo này có thể bị lộ, làm suy yếu toàn bộ cơ chế bảo vệ. Một phương pháp khác là mô hình cookie gửi hai lần (Double Submit Cookie Pattern). Trong mô hình này, máy chủ gửi một mã thông báo CSRF dưới dạng một cookie và cùng một mã thông báo đó cũng được nhúng vào một trường ẩn trong biểu mẫu hoặc tiêu đề của yêu cầu. Khi yêu cầu được gửi, JavaScript đọc giá trị cookie và đưa nó vào yêu cầu. Máy chủ sau đó xác minh rằng giá trị trong cookie khớp với giá trị trong yêu cầu. Ưu điểm chính của phương pháp này là tính phi trạng thái ở phía máy chủ, nhưng nó vẫn yêu cầu JavaScript ở phía client để đọc và gửi mã thông báo, và có thể dễ bị tổn thương nếu có lỗ hổng trong cấu hình miền phụ. Ngoài ra, việc sử dụng thuộc tính SameSite cho cookie đã nổi lên như một biện pháp phòng vệ cấp độ trình duyệt quan trọng. Thuộc tính SameSite cho phép máy chủ chỉ định liệu cookie có nên được gửi cùng với các yêu cầu chéo nguồn hay không. Với các giá trị như `Lax`, `Strict`, và `None`, nó cung cấp một lớp bảo vệ mạnh mẽ bằng cách hạn chế việc trình duyệt tự động gửi cookie phiên trong các yêu cầu chéo nguồn. `SameSite=Strict` ngăn chặn việc gửi cookie hoàn toàn trong các yêu cầu chéo nguồn, kể cả khi điều hướng cấp cao nhất, trong khi `SameSite=Lax` cho phép gửi cookie trong một số trường hợp nhất định (ví dụ: điều hướng GET cấp cao nhất). Mặc dù `SameSite` cookies là một biện pháp phòng thủ hiệu quả và dễ triển khai, chúng không phải là giải pháp độc lập hoàn hảo. Chúng có thể không hoạt động trên các trình duyệt cũ không hỗ trợ tính năng này hoặc có thể bị bỏ qua trong một số tình huống cụ thể nếu kẻ tấn công có thể kiểm soát nguồn gốc của yêu cầu. Do đó, việc kết hợp SameSite cookies với các cơ chế bảo vệ dựa trên mã thông báo vẫn là phương pháp tốt nhất. Các framework JavaScript hiện đại như React, Angular và Vue.js thường cung cấp các tiện ích hoặc tích hợp với các thư viện back-end để đơn giản hóa việc triển khai các biện pháp chống CSRF. Ví dụ, Angular có sẵn mô-đun `HttpClient` hỗ trợ tích hợp với cơ chế XSRF token. Tuy nhiên, trách nhiệm cuối cùng vẫn thuộc về nhà phát triển để đảm bảo rằng các biện pháp này được cấu hình đúng cách và được áp dụng xuyên suốt toàn bộ ứng dụng. Việc bỏ qua một điểm cuối API hoặc một biểu mẫu có thể tạo ra một lỗ hổng đáng kể. Một số phương pháp phòng chống khác bao gồm kiểm tra tiêu đề Referer, nhưng phương pháp này không đáng tin cậy do các vấn đề về quyền riêng tư và proxy có thể làm thay đổi hoặc loại bỏ tiêu đề này. Hơn nữa, việc yêu cầu xác nhận của người dùng cho các hành động nhạy cảm cũng có thể giảm thiểu rủi ro CSRF. Tóm lại, việc bảo vệ ứng dụng JavaScript khỏi CSRF đòi hỏi một chiến lược đa tầng, kết hợp các kỹ thuật từ phía máy chủ và phía máy khách, bao gồm mã thông báo xác thực, cấu hình cookie SameSite phù hợp, và việc giáo dục nhà phát triển về các mối đe dọa tiềm ẩn. Mặc dù các framework cung cấp các công cụ hữu ích, việc hiểu rõ các nguyên tắc cơ bản của CSRF và triển khai một cách cẩn thận là chìa khóa để xây dựng các ứng dụng web an toàn và đáng tin cậy trong môi trường ngày càng phức tạp.

text: Abstract: Survival models are crucial in applications like cancer treatment protocol development, yet many existing models focus primarily on prediction accuracy while neglecting calibrated uncertainty estimates. This oversight renders current models opaque and untrustworthy, as they can exhibit high confidence on dissimilar test cases and incorrect predictions. We introduce a Bayesian framework for survival models that enhances both the accuracy of survival predictions and the quantification of associated uncertainties. Our methodology integrates variational inference for uncertainty estimation, neural multi-task logistic regression to model nonlinear and time-varying risks, and a sparsity-inducing prior to handle high-dimensional data effectively. This novel combination addresses the deficiencies of traditional models, offering a more transparent and reliable approach to survival analysis.

text:
This paper addresses the challenge of estimating dense scene flow, which captures the 3D motion of objects in a scene, by leveraging stereo disparity and optical flow. The objective is to improve the accuracy and robustness of scene flow estimation, which is critical for applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. We propose a novel framework that integrates stereo disparity maps and optical flow fields to compute dense scene flow in real-world environments. Our approach combines a deep learning-based disparity estimation model with a state-of-the-art optical flow algorithm, enabling precise alignment of 3D motion vectors across consecutive frames. The proposed method is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing techniques. Key findings reveal that our framework achieves a significant reduction in error rates while maintaining real-time processing capabilities. The results highlight the potential of our approach for applications requiring high-fidelity motion estimation in dynamic scenes. This work contributes to advancing scene flow estimation by providing a scalable and efficient solution that bridges the gap between stereo vision and motion analysis.  

**Keywords**: dense scene flow, stereo disparity, optical flow, 3D motion estimation, deep learning, autonomous systems.
