text: 147-word abstract: Motivated by the need for complex modeling of conditional random fields (CRFs) via a Turing complete language and a convenient method for comparing generative-discriminative model pairs, going beyond typical graphical model specifications, this paper proposes a unified approach specifying CRFs generatively using probabilistic logic programs. Our approach involves implementing D-PRISM, a modification of PRISM leveraging its dynamic programming for efficiency, and introducing new CRF models: CRF-BNCs (CRF versions of Bayesian network classifiers) and CRF-LCGs (CRF versions of probabilistic left-corner grammars). Experiments with logistic regression, a linear-chain CRF, and a CRF-CFG empirically confirmed their excellent discriminative performance compared to their generative counterparts, i.e.\ naive Bayes, an HMM and a PCFG; furthermore, the new CRF-BNCs and CRF-LCGs also empirically outperformed their generative counterparts as expected. This work enables future research into more complex CRF architectures and facilitates broader application of the D-PRISM framework for generative-discriminative model comparison and development.

Kết quả chính cho thấy thang đo từng thành phần có độ tin cậy cao (hoạt động giảng dạy: 0,885; hành chính học vụ: 0,915; khuôn viên phòng học: 0,831; dịch vụ tăng thêm: 0,770), phân tích CFA xác nhận thang đo đảm bảo tính giá trị nội dung, giá trị cấu trúc và giá trị tiêu chí, đồng thời mô hình SEM chỉ ra thang đo giải thích được 79,3% biến thiên của sự hài lòng. Những phát hiện này khẳng định thang đo có tính giá trị và độ tin cậy tốt, đóng góp một công cụ đo lường đáng tin cậy cho việc đánh giá sự hài lòng của sinh viên khối cử nhân, từ đó hỗ trợ các nghiên cứu và hoạt động cải tiến chất lượng dịch vụ đào tạo trong tương lai.

text: Gastrocolic fistula is an uncommon clinical entity characterized by an abnormal communication between the stomach and the colon, with etiologies that can be either benign or malignant. A 54-year-old male patient, diagnosed with colon cancer, was admitted presenting with prolonged diarrhea, fecaloid vomiting, and weight loss. Computed tomography (CT) scan results revealed the presence of a fistulous tract between the stomach and the colon. However, surgical resection of the fistula was not considered an option for this patient. Various medical interventions aimed at mitigating persistent diarrhea proved unsuccessful; octreotide demonstrated some improvement in this case, yet its prohibitive cost limited its sustained use. Malignant gastrocolic fistula typically results from the invasion of a malignant tumor originating from either the stomach or the colon and is associated with a poor prognosis. Therapeutic approaches may be curative, such as en bloc resection, or palliative, encompassing fluid and electrolyte repletion, parenteral nutrition, and the management of diarrhea—a distressing complication that causes significant patient discomfort and leads to metabolic and hydroelectrolytic derangements.

text: This paper proposes a novel deep learning approach for building change detection in remote sensing images, leveraging a dual task constrained deep Siamese convolutional network model. The objective is to accurately identify changes in buildings between two multitemporal images, addressing the challenges of varying environmental conditions and image quality. Our method employs a Siamese network architecture, where two identical convolutional neural networks are trained to learn feature representations from input image pairs. A dual task constraint is introduced, combining change detection and image similarity measurement, to enhance the model's ability to distinguish between changed and unchanged regions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed model achieves a significant improvement in change detection performance, particularly in scenarios with complex backgrounds and varying illumination conditions. This research contributes to the development of advanced remote sensing image analysis techniques, with potential applications in urban planning, disaster response, and environmental monitoring. Key keywords: building change detection, remote sensing, deep Siamese convolutional network, dual task constraint, image analysis.

Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện trên bệnh nhân đến Phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ tại Phòng Khám KAT và Bệnh viện Thẩm mỹ Thanh Vân từ tháng 1 năm 2018 đến tháng 6 năm 2019. Phương pháp lấy mẫu thuận tiện với bảng câu hỏi tự thiết kế. Nhập liệu và quản lý số liệu bằng Phần mềm Epidata, phân tích số liệu bằng phần mềm SPSS 14. Kết quả: Mẫu nghiên cứu gồm 1684 đối tượng, nữ chiếm 95,61%. Đa số các bệnh nhân đều trên 18 tuổi và 1/3 bệnh nhân đã từng phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ trước đây. Nhu cầu phẫu thuật mắt và mũi trong nghiên cứu này lần lượt là 80,70% và 22,44%. Cắt da bỏ da thừa vùng mắt, mí tự nhiên và chỉnh hình mũi Sline là những nhu cầu có tỷ lệ cao nhất. Bệnh nhân trên 18 tuổi có nhu cầu phẫu thuật mắt cao hơn, trong khi những người dưới 18 tuổi có nhu cầu phẫu thuật mũi. Nhu cầu phẫu thuật mắt và mũi ở những bệnh nhân có tiền sử phẫu thuật cao hơn những người chưa từng thực hiện, và sự khác biệt này có ý nghĩa thống kê với p < 0,05. Kết luận: Nhu cầu phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ mắt cao hơn mũi. Các yếu tố liên quan đến nhu cầu phẫu thuật gồm có tuổi và tiền sử phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ.

Additionally, the influence of illumination conditions on the perceived color of pH strips was examined, and further experiments were conducted to study the effect of color change on the learning model. Test results using JPEG, RAW, and RAW-corrected image formats captured under different lighting conditions demonstrated perfect classification accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, indicating that colorimetric detection using machine learning-based systems is highly adaptable to various experimental conditions and represents a promising candidate for smartphone-based sensing in paper-based colorimetric assays.

text: Incorporating nonlinearity is paramount to predicting the future states of a dynamical system, its response to shocks, and its underlying causal network. However, most existing methods for causality detection and impulse response, such as Vector Autoregression (VAR), assume linearity and are thus unable to capture the complexity. Here, we introduce a vector autoencoder nonlinear autoregression neural network (VANAR) capable of both automatic time series feature extraction for its inputs and functional form estimation. We evaluate VANAR in three ways: first in terms of pure forecast accuracy, second in terms of detecting the correct causality between variables, and lastly in terms of impulse response where we model trajectories given external shocks. These tests were performed on a simulated nonlinear chaotic system and an empirical system using Philippine macroeconomic data. Results show that VANAR significantly outperforms VAR in the forecast and causality tests. VANAR has consistently superior accuracy even over state of the art models such as SARIMA and TBATS. For the impulse response test, both models fail to predict the shocked trajectories of the nonlinear chaotic system. VANAR was robust in its ability to model a wide variety of dynamics, from chaotic, high noise, and low data environments to macroeconomic systems.
label: human-text

text: Recent advancements in neural networks have enabled them to effectively participate in dialogues, but existing methods are limited to verbal text and neglect the nuances of in-person conversations. Our approach utilizes an RNN encoder-decoder that leverages both facial muscle movements and verbal dialogue. The decoder features a two-layer architecture, where the first layer generates verbal responses and coarse facial expressions, and the second layer refines these outputs by adding subtle gestures, resulting in more natural and smooth interactions. Trained on a dataset of 250 movies, our neural network is evaluated through automated metrics and a human study, demonstrating its capability to produce more realistic conversations. text: Given the significant success of deep learning in visual tasks, representations extracted from intermediate layers of learned models, i.e., deep features, have garnered substantial research attention. Prior empirical analyses indicate that these features can possess pertinent semantic information; consequently, features extracted from models trained on large-scale benchmark datasets (e.g., ImageNet) often demonstrate effective performance on disparate tasks. This work investigates this phenomenon, demonstrating that deep features can be suboptimal as they are acquired through the minimization of empirical risk. The performance of deep features may degrade when the data distribution of the target task diverges from that of the benchmark dataset. Hence, a hierarchically robust optimization method is proposed to learn more generalizable features. Simultaneously considering example-level and concept-level robustness, the problem is formulated as a distributionally robust optimization problem incorporating Wasserstein ambiguity set constraints, for which an efficient algorithm compatible with the conventional training pipeline is proposed. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the robust deep representations.

text: Bộ điều phối (Scheduler). Đây là thành phần lập lịch chịu trách nhiệm quản lý các spyder. Nó đảm bảo rằng các spyder không tải quá nhiều các trang web và có thể xử lý lỗi xảy ra trong quá trình thu thập dữ liệu. Để đạt được mục tiêu này, Bộ điều phối thực hiện một loạt các chức năng phức tạp, bao gồm quản lý hàng đợi URL, thực thi chính sách lịch sự (politeness policy) và tối ưu hóa việc sử dụng tài nguyên. Về chính sách lịch sự, Scheduler tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt các quy tắc được định nghĩa trong tệp `robots.txt` của mỗi trang web, đặt ra các khoảng thời gian chờ (crawl delay) giữa các yêu cầu liên tiếp đến cùng một tên miền, đồng thời áp dụng giới hạn tỷ lệ (rate limiting) để ngăn chặn việc gây quá tải cho máy chủ mục tiêu. Điều này không chỉ giúp duy trì mối quan hệ tốt với các quản trị viên web mà còn tránh nguy cơ bị chặn IP hoặc đưa vào danh sách đen do các hành vi thu thập dữ liệu quá hung hãn. Trong trường hợp xảy ra lỗi trong quá trình thu thập dữ liệu, Bộ điều phối đóng vai trò thiết yếu trong việc xác định loại lỗi (ví dụ: lỗi mạng tạm thời, lỗi máy chủ, hoặc lỗi nội dung) và áp dụng các chiến lược phục hồi phù hợp. Các chiến lược này có thể bao gồm việc thử lại yêu cầu sau một khoảng thời gian nhất định với cơ chế lũy thừa gián đoạn (exponential backoff), đánh dấu các URL hoặc tên miền không thể truy cập để tránh truy vấn lại chúng trong tương lai gần, hoặc chuyển hướng các yêu cầu lỗi đến một hàng đợi xử lý riêng để phân tích nguyên nhân sâu hơn. Một chức năng cốt lõi khác của Bộ điều phối là quản lý hàng đợi URL (URL frontier). Hàng đợi này lưu trữ tất cả các URL cần được thu thập, bao gồm cả những URL mới được phát hiện và những URL cần được ghé thăm lại. Scheduler phải sử dụng các thuật toán hiệu quả để duy trì hàng đợi này, ví dụ như sử dụng cấu trúc dữ liệu dựa trên ưu tiên (priority queue) để phân loại các URL dựa trên các tiêu chí như độ sâu của liên kết, mức độ quan trọng của trang, tần suất cập nhật dự kiến, hoặc loại nội dung. Việc loại bỏ các URL trùng lặp (duplicate URLs) là một nhiệm vụ quan trọng khác được thực hiện bởi Bộ điều phối, thường thông qua việc sử dụng hàm băm (hashing) hoặc bộ lọc Bloom (Bloom filter) để đảm bảo tính duy nhất và tránh lãng phí tài nguyên mạng và lưu trữ. Ngoài ra, trong các hệ thống thu thập dữ liệu phân tán quy mô lớn, Bộ điều phối còn chịu trách nhiệm điều phối hoạt động của nhiều thực thể spyder chạy song song. Nó phân bổ các nhiệm vụ thu thập dữ liệu một cách thông minh giữa các spyder, cân bằng tải và giám sát trạng thái hoạt động của chúng. Điều này bao gồm việc theo dõi hiệu suất của từng spyder, phát hiện các spyder bị treo hoặc hoạt động bất thường, và tự động gán lại các nhiệm vụ chưa hoàn thành. Sự hiệu quả của Bộ điều phối ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến tốc độ, phạm vi và độ tin cậy của toàn bộ quá trình thu thập dữ liệu. Nó không chỉ là một cơ chế phòng vệ chống lại việc lạm dụng tài nguyên web mà còn là một bộ não chiến lược, quyết định thứ tự và cách thức khám phá không gian mạng rộng lớn, đảm bảo rằng dữ liệu được thu thập là mới nhất, đầy đủ nhất và có giá trị nhất cho mục đích nghiên cứu hoặc ứng dụng.

text: Trong số các phương pháp đo nhãn áp, tonometry là kỹ thuật phổ biến nhất, với nhiều biến thể như applanation tonometry, non-contact tonometry và rebound tonometry. Mỗi phương pháp có những ưu và nhược điểm riêng, do đó việc lựa chọn phương pháp phù hợp phụ thuộc vào tình trạng lâm sàng cụ thể và khả năng tiếp cận của bệnh nhân. Applanation tonometry, chẳng hạn, được xem là tiêu chuẩn vàng trong đo nhãn áp nhờ độ chính xác cao, nhưng yêu cầu tiếp xúc trực tiếp với giác mạc và thường cần sử dụng thuốc gây tê. Ngược lại, non-contact tonometry, còn được gọi là "air puff" tonometry, không đòi hỏi tiếp xúc vật lý và do đó giảm nguy cơ lây nhiễm, nhưng có thể kém chính xác hơn trong một số trường hợp. Trong khi đó, rebound tonometry cung cấp một giải pháp trung gian với sự tiện lợi và độ chính xác tương đối, đặc biệt hữu ích trong môi trường lâm sàng di động hoặc với các bệnh nhân trẻ tuổi. Hơn nữa, các nghiên cứu gần đây đã tập trung vào việc phát triển các thiết bị đo nhãn áp liên tục nhằm cung cấp dữ liệu động về biến thiên nhãn áp trong suốt 24 giờ, từ đó cung cấp cái nhìn toàn diện hơn về tình trạng nhãn áp của bệnh nhân. Sự tiến bộ trong công nghệ y sinh học, cùng với hiểu biết sâu sắc hơn về cơ chế sinh lý bệnh liên quan đến nhãn áp, hứa hẹn mang lại những cải tiến đáng kể trong việc chẩn đoán, theo dõi và điều trị các bệnh lý liên quan đến nhãn áp.

text: It is crucial to systematically organize and arrange goods within a warehouse, as this practice offers significant benefits to businesses, including reduced storage expenses, enhanced managerial efficiency, improved inventory rotation, and lower operational costs. However, many companies still fail to prioritize the optimization and management of their storage layouts. Determining when the need to implement a warehouse island process arises and when it is justified remains a critical consideration. Warehouses often house a large volume of items with complex classifications, requiring goods to be sorted by size, expiration date, and specific storage requirements based on their type. Identifying the appropriate storage locations for each category of goods is vital to ensuring safety and streamlining the storage and movement processes. Additionally, consistent monitoring of product locations within the warehouse is essential to facilitate necessary adjustments, thereby minimizing risks associated with inventory management.

text:
This paper introduces a novel end-to-end framework for super-resolution (SR) from raw image bursts, leveraging the principles of the Lucas-Kanade algorithm to enhance image reconstruction. The objective is to address the limitations of traditional SR methods, which often struggle with noise, motion artifacts, and computational inefficiency when processing burst images. Our approach integrates a deep learning-based pipeline that directly processes raw sensor data, combining optical flow estimation with a multi-frame fusion mechanism to align and merge burst frames effectively. The proposed model employs a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, optimized for both accuracy and computational efficiency, enabling real-time performance on resource-constrained devices. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly in scenarios with complex motion and low-light conditions. The framework also exhibits robustness to varying noise levels and motion blur, making it suitable for practical applications such as mobile photography and medical imaging. This work contributes a scalable and efficient solution for burst-based SR, bridging the gap between classical computer vision techniques and modern deep learning approaches.  

**Keywords**: super-resolution, Lucas-Kanade, raw image bursts, optical flow, deep learning, multi-frame fusion, computational efficiency.

Although the employed loss functions do not explicitly penalize control energy, the NODEC framework is shown to generate low-energy control signals. Finally, the performance and versatility of NODEC are demonstrated through its application in controlling a system comprising over one thousand coupled, non-linear ODEs.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of off-policy evaluation in recommendation systems, where the goal is to estimate the performance of a new policy without deploying it. The objective is to develop a debiased off-policy evaluation method that accurately estimates the expected reward of a target policy using historical data collected from a different behavior policy. We propose a novel approach that combines inverse propensity scoring with a neural network-based estimator to reduce bias and variance in off-policy evaluation. Our method, dubbed Debiased Off-Policy Evaluation (DOPE), uses a multi-task learning framework to learn both the propensity scores and the expected reward simultaneously. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that DOPE outperforms state-of-the-art off-policy evaluation methods, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include a debiased off-policy evaluation method, a multi-task learning framework, and a comprehensive evaluation framework for recommendation systems. This work has important implications for the development of more effective and efficient recommendation systems, and can be applied to various domains such as e-commerce, online advertising, and content recommendation. Key keywords: off-policy evaluation, recommendation systems, debiasing, inverse propensity scoring, neural networks, multi-task learning.

Understanding the decision-making processes of complex machine learning models, often referred to as "black-box" systems, remains a critical challenge in artificial intelligence. This paper introduces a novel counterfactual approach to explain the behavior of black-box models in a smooth and interpretable manner. The proposed method generates counterfactual explanations by identifying minimal changes to input features that lead to a desired output, enabling users to understand model predictions without requiring access to internal model parameters. Leveraging optimization techniques and gradient-based methods, the approach ensures that counterfactuals are both realistic and actionable, addressing limitations of existing explanation frameworks. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in providing intuitive and robust explanations, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques in terms of plausibility and computational efficiency. The findings highlight the potential of this approach to enhance transparency and trust in AI systems, with applications in healthcare, finance, and other domains where interpretability is crucial.

text: While local windows in computer vision are conventionally centered on the pixels being processed, we demonstrate this standard practice is not universally optimal, particularly because centering the window on an edge pixel is a primary cause of edge blurring in many filtering algorithms. To address this, we introduce the Side Window Filtering (SWF) technique, which instead aligns the window's side or corner with the processed pixel. This surprisingly simple, theoretically grounded, and practically effective SWF technique facilitates the easy implementation of many traditional linear and nonlinear filters. Extensive analysis and experiments reveal that applying the SWF principle markedly enhances their edge-preserving capabilities, leading to state-of-the-art results in applications such as image smoothing, denoising, enhancement, structure-preserving texture-removing, mutual-structure extraction, and HDR tone mapping. Furthermore, the SWF principle extends beyond image filtering to other local window-based applications; for instance, using colorization by optimization as an example, we demonstrate its effectiveness in preventing artifacts like color leakage associated with conventional implementations. Given the ubiquity of window-based operations in computer vision, the novel SWF technique is poised to benefit a broad range of additional applications.
label: human---gemini-text

This paper addresses the challenge of generating reliable process event streams and time series data, which are critical for testing and validating process mining algorithms and predictive models. Traditional methods often fail to capture the complexity and variability of real-world processes, leading to limited generalizability. To overcome this, we propose a novel approach leveraging neural networks, specifically designed to model and simulate realistic event streams and time series data. Our method integrates advanced architectures, such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformers, to capture temporal dependencies and intricate patterns inherent in process data. The proposed framework is evaluated on synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its ability to generate high-fidelity data that closely mirrors real process behaviors. Results show significant improvements in data quality and reliability compared to existing techniques, with enhanced performance in downstream tasks such as anomaly detection and predictive analytics. The study contributes a robust, scalable solution for generating process data, enabling more accurate testing and development of process mining tools. This work has broad implications for industries relying on process optimization, including manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics.  

**Keywords**: process mining, event streams, time series data, neural networks, RNNs, transformers, data generation, predictive analytics.

text: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in a range of prediction tasks across static graphs, yet many real-world networks are inherently dynamic, with evolving structures and attributes over time. Addressing the challenge of learning effective node representations in such time-varying graphs, the Temporal Multilayered Position-aware Graph Neural Network (TMP-GNN) is introduced as a novel node embedding approach that explicitly models the interdependence of temporal relations within dynamic graphs. TMP-GNN’s architecture captures both the multilayered nature and temporal dependencies of dynamic networks, enhancing the expressiveness of node embeddings for downstream tasks. The model is rigorously evaluated on two distinct temporal multilayered graph representations and benchmarked against leading GNN variants in node-level prediction scenarios. Furthermore, TMP-GNN is integrated into a deep learning framework for missing data estimation, with comparative analyses against established GNNs and a baseline approach. Empirical results from four real-world datasets demonstrate substantial improvements, with TMP-GNN achieving up to a 58% reduction in ROC AUC for pairwise node classification and up to a 96% decrease in MAE for missing feature estimation, particularly excelling in graphs characterized by larger node counts and lower average connectivity. These findings underscore TMP-GNN's effectiveness for dynamic graph representation learning and inference tasks.

text: Object detection is a critical component in various visual applications. However, a common challenge lies in the trade-off between detection precision and speed, where fast detectors often suffer from reduced accuracy, particularly when dealing with small objects. To address this limitation, we introduce the Multiple Receptive Field and Small-Object-Focusing Weakly-Supervised Segmentation Network (MRFSWSnet) for achieving rapid object detection. MRFSWSnet incorporates a Multiple Receptive Fields (MRF) block designed to enhance feature discriminability by applying varying weights to different spatial regions of both the object and its surrounding background. Furthermore, to improve the accuracy of small object detection, a specialized weakly-supervised segmentation module, which specifically targets small objects rather than all objects, is integrated into the detection network for auxiliary training. Extensive experiments on the PASCAL VOC and MS COCO detection datasets confirm the efficacy of our method. Notably, using a lower resolution input (300x300), MRFSWSnet achieves an 80.9% mAP on the VOC2007 test set with an impressive inference speed of 15 milliseconds per frame, positioning it as a state-of-the-art real-time detector.

text: A dynamic texture (DT) refers to a sequence of images that exhibit temporal regularities and has many applications in computer vision and graphics. Given an exemplar of dynamic texture, it is a dynamic but challenging task to generate new samples with high quality that are perceptually similar to the input exemplar, which is known to be . Numerous approaches have been devoted to this problem, in the past decades, but none them are able to tackle all kinds of dynamic textures equally well. In this paper, we investigate the synthesizability of dynamic texture samples:  To this end, we propose to learn regression models to connect dynamic texture samples with synthesizability scores, with the help of a compiled dynamic texture dataset annotated in terms of synthesizability. More precisely, we first define the synthesizability of DT samples and characterize them by a set of spatiotemporal features. Based on these features and an annotated dynamic texture dataset, we then train regression models to predict the synthesizability scores of texture samples and learn classifiers to select the most suitable EDTS methods. We further complete the selection, partition and synthesizability prediction of dynamic texture samples in a hierarchical scheme. We finally apply the learned synthesizability to detecting synthesizable regions in videos. The experiments demonstrate that our method can effectively learn and predict the synthesizability of DT samples.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of efficient context vector inference in sequence-to-sequence networks, a crucial component in various natural language processing tasks. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that reduces the computational cost associated with context vector inference, thereby improving the overall performance of sequence-to-sequence models. We propose an amortized context vector inference method, which leverages a learned prior distribution to approximate the context vector. Our approach utilizes a variational autoencoder-based framework to learn a probabilistic representation of the context vector, allowing for efficient inference and generation of sequences. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves significant improvements in inference speed and accuracy compared to existing approaches. The proposed technique has important implications for applications such as machine translation, text summarization, and chatbots, where efficient sequence-to-sequence processing is critical. Key contributions of this research include the introduction of amortized context vector inference and the demonstration of its effectiveness in sequence-to-sequence networks, with potential applications in AI, NLP, and deep learning. text: Smart home systems enhance residents' quality of life by utilizing sensors and actuators to automate tasks, with many actions relying on activity recognition models. However, imperfect recognition accuracy can cause unexpected behaviors, prompting users to question system decisions. This research leverages Explainable AI (XAI) principles to develop methods for clarifying activity classifications in smart homes. We propose four computational techniques for producing natural language explanations from smart home data and assess their effectiveness. A user study reveals that SHAP-based explanations achieve 92% accuracy, while 84% of participants favor detailed explanations over basic activity labels, highlighting the demand for transparency. Additionally, certain XAI methods influence user trust—some diminish confidence in the recognition model, while others strengthen it. Based on these findings, we identify the most suitable XAI approach for smart home automation and outline directions for future research.

text:
Và trò cụ thể của các package trong mô hình như sau:

**Controller Package** chịu trách nhiệm chính trong việc tiếp nhận các yêu cầu từ phía Frontend, đóng vai trò như cổng vào của hệ thống Backend. Nhiệm vụ của Controller là phân tích yêu cầu HTTP, thực hiện các kiểm tra xác thực và kiểm tra đầu vào cơ bản, sau đó điều phối yêu cầu đến tầng xử lý nghiệp vụ phù hợp. Controller không chứa logic nghiệp vụ phức tạp mà tập trung vào việc định tuyến, chuyển đổi dữ liệu đầu vào và gọi các phương thức tương ứng từ tầng Business. Sau khi tầng Business hoàn tất xử lý và trả về kết quả, Controller sẽ có trách nhiệm định dạng dữ liệu đầu ra (thường là JSON) và gửi phản hồi trở lại cho Frontend. Sự tách biệt này đảm bảo rằng Controller luôn giữ vai trò mỏng (thin controller), giúp code dễ đọc, dễ bảo trì và dễ kiểm thử hơn, đồng thời giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc lẫn nhau giữa các thành phần.

**Business Package (còn được gọi là Service Layer hoặc Logic Layer)** là trái tim của hệ thống Backend, chứa đựng toàn bộ các quy tắc nghiệp vụ và logic xử lý cốt lõi của ứng dụng. Đây là nơi các thao tác phức tạp được thực hiện, ví dụ như tính toán, kiểm tra ràng buộc nghiệp vụ sâu hơn, quản lý các giao dịch phức tạp liên quan đến nhiều thực thể dữ liệu, hoặc tích hợp với các hệ thống bên ngoài. Tầng Business nhận dữ liệu từ Controller, xử lý theo logic đã định, và sau đó tương tác với tầng Model để truy xuất hoặc lưu trữ dữ liệu vào cơ sở dữ liệu. Mọi quyết định về cách thức dữ liệu được xử lý, thay đổi trạng thái, và tương tác giữa các thực thể đều được định nghĩa rõ ràng tại đây. Mục tiêu chính của tầng Business là đảm bảo tính nhất quán, toàn vẹn và đúng đắn của dữ liệu cũng như các quy trình nghiệp vụ. Việc tách biệt logic nghiệp vụ vào một tầng riêng biệt giúp tăng khả năng tái sử dụng code, dễ dàng mở rộng và quan trọng nhất là dễ dàng kiểm thử các quy tắc nghiệp vụ một cách độc lập mà không cần phụ thuộc vào tầng giao diện hay tầng truy cập dữ liệu.

**Model Package** đại diện cho cấu trúc dữ liệu và các thao tác liên quan đến cơ sở dữ liệu. Trong mô hình này, Model thường được chia thành hai phần chính: Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) hoặc Plain Old Java Objects (POJOs)/Plain Old CLR Objects (POCOs) đại diện cho cấu trúc của các thực thể dữ liệu, và Data Access Objects (DAOs) hoặc Repositories chịu trách nhiệm tương tác trực tiếp với cơ sở dữ liệu. Tầng Model cung cấp các phương thức để thực hiện các thao tác CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) dữ liệu, ánh xạ dữ liệu từ cơ sở dữ liệu sang các đối tượng lập trình và ngược lại. Nhiệm vụ của Model là cung cấp một lớp trừu tượng hóa cho việc truy cập dữ liệu, giúp tầng Business không cần phải quan tâm đến chi tiết kỹ thuật của cơ sở dữ liệu (ví dụ: loại cơ sở dữ liệu, câu lệnh SQL cụ thể). Tầng Model không chứa logic nghiệp vụ; nó chỉ tập trung vào việc quản lý và cung cấp dữ liệu một cách hiệu quả và an toàn. Việc tách biệt tầng Model giúp hệ thống dễ dàng thay đổi loại cơ sở dữ liệu hoặc cấu trúc dữ liệu mà không ảnh hưởng đến logic nghiệp vụ, đồng thời cải thiện khả năng bảo trì và kiểm thử của phần mềm.

Sự phân chia rõ ràng các gói Controller, Business và Model trong mô hình Backend này không chỉ giúp tổ chức mã nguồn một cách có hệ thống, mà còn mang lại nhiều lợi ích quan trọng về kiến trúc. Nó thúc đẩy nguyên tắc tách biệt các mối quan tâm (separation of concerns), mỗi package có một vai trò và trách nhiệm cụ thể, độc lập với các package khác. Điều này giúp nâng cao khả năng đọc hiểu mã nguồn, giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc giữa các module, từ đó cải thiện đáng kể khả năng bảo trì và mở rộng hệ thống. Khi có sự thay đổi về yêu cầu nghiệp vụ, chỉ cần điều chỉnh trong tầng Business; khi giao diện người dùng thay đổi, chỉ cần thay đổi Frontend và Controller; và khi cấu trúc cơ sở dữ liệu thay đổi, chỉ cần cập nhật tầng Model. Hơn nữa, kiến trúc này còn tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho việc kiểm thử đơn vị (unit testing) và kiểm thử tích hợp (integration testing) cho từng thành phần một cách độc lập, đảm bảo chất lượng và độ tin cậy của phần mềm. Cuối cùng, việc này cũng hỗ trợ việc phân chia công việc trong các nhóm phát triển lớn, cho phép các lập trình viên tập trung vào các tầng khác nhau mà không ảnh hưởng lẫn nhau, nâng cao hiệu suất làm việc và tốc độ phát triển dự án.

Các thao tác này bao gồm loại bỏ ký tự đặc biệt, chuẩn hóa khoảng trắng, chuyển đổi văn bản sang chữ thường và loại bỏ các từ dừng (stop words) như "the," "and," "s," v.v., nhằm nâng cao hiệu quả phân tích và xử lý dữ liệu văn bản. Tiếp theo, Auto Phrase ứng dụng các kỹ thuật Xử lý Ngôn ngữ Tự nhiên (NLP) để phân tích và nhận diện các cụm từ trong văn bản. Các kỹ thuật này bao gồm tokenization (tách từ), part of speech tagging (gán nhãn loại từ) và syntactic parsing (phân tích cú pháp), giúp hệ thống nắm bắt cấu trúc ngữ pháp và ngữ nghĩa của câu. Sau khi dữ liệu đã được tiền xử lý và phân tích NLP, Auto Phrase sử dụng một mô hình học máy để đánh giá mức độ quan trọng của các cụm từ trong văn bản. Mô hình này được huấn luyện dựa trên tập dữ liệu đã được gán nhãn, trong đó các cụm từ có mức độ quan trọng cao đã được đánh dấu. Dựa trên kết quả từ mô hình học máy, Auto Phrase tiến hành nhận diện các cụm từ có ý nghĩa từ vựng nổi bật trong văn bản. Những cụm từ này được đánh giá là có ý nghĩa và khả năng biểu đạt cao hơn so với các từ đơn lẻ. Cuối cùng, các cụm từ có ý nghĩa từ vựng này cho phép Auto Phrase thực hiện các tác vụ xử lý ngôn ngữ tự động nâng cao như gán nhãn, phân loại hoặc trích xuất thông tin từ văn bản một cách hiệu quả.

CRATOS contributes to the field by offering a reliable, scalable, and domain-agnostic solution for time-series analysis, paving the way for future advancements in predictive analytics.

The original text: In performative prediction, predictions guide decision-making and hence can influence the distribution of future data. To date, work on performative prediction has focused on finding performatively stable models, which are the fixed points of repeated retraining. However, stable solutions can be far from optimal when evaluated in terms of the performative risk, the loss experienced by the decision maker when deploying a model. In this paper, we shift attention beyond performative stability and focus on optimizing the performative risk directly. We identify a natural set of properties of the loss function and model-induced distribution shift under which the performative risk is convex, a property which does not follow from convexity of the loss alone. Furthermore, we develop algorithms that leverage our structural assumptions to optimize the performative risk with better sample efficiency than generic methods for derivative-free convex optimization.

Optimizing Performative Risk addresses a critical limitation in performative prediction: existing work prioritizes performative stability, yet stable models often fail to minimize the actual performative risk experienced by decision-makers. This paper shifts focus to directly optimizing the performative risk. We identify a set of natural properties for loss functions and model-induced distribution shifts that establish the convexity of performative risk, a non-trivial finding that extends beyond simple loss convexity. Building on this structural understanding, we contribute novel algorithms designed to optimize performative risk. These algorithms demonstrate superior sample efficiency compared to generic derivative-free convex optimization methods, offering a significant advancement in achieving truly optimal predictions in adaptive environments.

text: Recent research has explored methods for enhancing continual image classification by investigating the transferability of learned features through spectral decomposition in the representation space. Specifically, this study examines the sensitivity of spectral components by training a learner on two consecutive tasks and observing the adjustment of eigenvalues post-training of the second task. The dataset from the initial task is fed into two model versions: one trained solely on the first task and the other on both tasks. Spectral decomposition is then applied to these representation spaces to extract eigenvalues. Significant changes in eigenvectors after training on the second task indicate forgettable directions, as they alter the data distribution's shape. As depicted in Figure 3.9, the study compares eigenvalues before and after the second task using Corresponding Angles, formally defined in subsection 4.4. The research reveals that spectral components with large eigenvalues exhibit minimal changes and are thus deemed transferable. Leveraging this insight, a novel augmentation method, termed Dual Augmentation, is proposed. This method aims to expand spectral components to foster more diverse and transferable representations, enhancing incremental learning capabilities.

text: Instance segmentation on 3D point clouds is one of the most extensively researched areas toward the realization of autonomous cars and robots. Certain existing studies have split input point clouds into small regions such as 1m x 1m; one reason for this is that models in the studies cannot consume a large number of points because of the large space complexity. However, because such small regions occasionally include a very small number of instances belonging to the same class, an evaluation using existing metrics such as mAP is largely affected by the category recognition performance. To address these problems, we propose a new method with space complexity O(Np) such that large regions can be consumed, as well as novel metrics for tasks that are independent of the categories or size of the inputs. Our method learns a mapping from input point clouds to an embedding space, where the embeddings form clusters for each instance and distinguish instances using these clusters during testing. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance using both existing and the proposed metrics. Moreover, we show that our new metric can evaluate the performance of a task without being affected by any other condition.

text: Kernel-UCBVI addresses the exploration-exploitation dilemma in finite-horizon reinforcement learning by introducing a model-based optimistic algorithm that exploits the metric structure of the state-action space. This method harnesses the inherent smoothness of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) and applies a non-parametric kernel estimator to model both rewards and transition dynamics, thus facilitating efficient exploration and exploitation without the need for explicit partitioning of the state-action space. In contrast to previous algorithms that rely on discretization or partitioning and offer regret guarantees, Kernel-UCBVI achieves comparable performance through its kernel-based approach. Theoretical analysis establishes a regret bound of order O(H³K^(d+1)/(d+2)), where H is the episode horizon, K is the number of episodes, and d denotes the covering dimension of the joint state-action space. Empirical evaluations on both discrete and continuous MDPs further substantiate the effectiveness and generality of Kernel-UCBVI, demonstrating its capability to efficiently learn optimal policies while maintaining favorable regret performance across different environments.

text: The assessment report by Working Group I of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) issued in early 2013 asserts that climate change constitutes one of humanity’s most significant challenges, primarily driven by carbon emissions from human residential and production activities. text: Generally speaking, relation extraction is a multi-classification problem where learners are trained to predict the relationship between two given entities in a context. For example, given the entity pair [James Cameron, Titanic] in the sentence “Titanic is an epic romance film directed by James Cameron”, the classifier is expected to predict the relation the-director-of. While effective in static environments with predefined schemas, traditional relation extraction models face significant challenges when applied to dynamic real-world scenarios where new relations emerge frequently, and data continuously streams. This necessitates the adoption of Continual Relation Extraction, a paradigm designed to incrementally learn novel relation types and instances without necessitating retraining on the entire historical dataset. The primary challenge in Continual Relation Extraction, however, is catastrophic forgetting, where the model's performance on previously learned relations significantly degrades upon learning new ones. This phenomenon arises because new knowledge often interferes with the neural network's parameters optimized for past tasks. Addressing this, our work focuses on techniques to mitigate catastrophic forgetting by promoting feature decorrelation among different tasks, aiming to isolate and preserve discriminative features for each relation type, thereby enhancing knowledge retention and model adaptability in `Continual Relation Extraction with Feature Decorrelation`.

text: Deep learning’s remarkable achievements in visual tasks have led researchers to focus on deep features, the representations extracted from intermediate layers of trained models. Empirical studies have shown these features often capture valuable semantic information. As a result, features extracted from models trained on large-scale benchmark datasets (e.g., ImageNet) can perform effectively on other tasks. In this study, we further examine this phenomenon and show that deep features may be suboptimal because they are learned by minimizing empirical risk. When the data distribution of the target task diverges from that of the benchmark dataset, the performance of these deep features can decline. To address this, we introduce a hierarchically robust optimization approach to learn more generalizable features. By simultaneously considering robustness at both the example and concept levels, we cast the problem as a distributionally robust optimization task with Wasserstein ambiguity set constraints, and propose an efficient algorithm compatible with standard training pipelines. Experiments on benchmark datasets confirm the efficacy of our robust deep representations.

text: Although there is significant demand for automatic segmentation methods, current state-of-the-art deep learning segmentation techniques have yet to see widespread adoption in clinical practice. A key barrier is their lack of reliability, as these models can fail without detection and often generate anatomically implausible results that medical professionals would not produce. This paper introduces an automated image segmentation approach utilizing (Bayesian) dilated convolutional networks (DCNN) to produce both segmentation masks and spatial uncertainty maps for a given input image. The method was trained and tested on the segmentation of the left ventricle (LV) cavity, right ventricle (RV) endocardium, and myocardium (Myo) at end-diastole (ED) and end-systole (ES) using 100 cardiac 2D MR scans from the MICCAI 2017 Challenge (ACDC). By integrating segmentations and uncertainty maps in a human-in-the-loop framework, we demonstrate that regions identified as highly uncertain closely correspond to areas with segmentation errors. This combined information can be leveraged to enhance segmentation accuracy. Our findings show that DCNNs can efficiently generate valuable spatial uncertainty maps with minimal computational cost.

text: Kiến trúc Model-View-Controller (MVC) cung cấp một cơ chế phân tách rõ ràng giữa ba thành phần cốt lõi của một ứng dụng phần mềm: logic nghiệp vụ (Model), trình bày dữ liệu (View), và xử lý tương tác người dùng (Controller). Sự phân tách này, như đã được ghi nhận rộng rãi trong các công trình kinh điển (ví dụ, Krasner & Pope, 1988; Gamma et al., 1995), mang lại nhiều ưu điểm quan trọng, bao gồm việc tăng cường khả năng bảo trì, thúc đẩy tính tái sử dụng của các thành phần, và cho phép phát triển song song giữa các nhóm làm việc khác nhau. text:
The increasing reliance on object detection systems in critical applications such as autonomous driving and surveillance has highlighted the need to understand their vulnerabilities. This paper investigates the susceptibility of object detectors to adversarial examples—inputs specifically crafted to deceive machine learning models. We propose a novel method for generating adversarial examples that effectively fool state-of-the-art object detection systems, including both single-stage and two-stage detectors. Our approach leverages gradient-based optimization techniques to perturb input images in a way that causes detectors to misclassify or fail to detect objects entirely. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves high success rates across multiple datasets and detector architectures, significantly outperforming existing adversarial attack techniques. Furthermore, we analyze the transferability of these adversarial examples across different models, revealing insights into the robustness of object detection systems. Our findings underscore the importance of developing more robust detection frameworks and highlight potential risks in deploying these systems in safety-critical environments. This work contributes to the growing body of research on adversarial machine learning by providing a deeper understanding of the vulnerabilities in object detection systems and proposing a practical framework for evaluating their robustness.  

**Keywords**: adversarial examples, object detection, machine learning, robustness, gradient-based optimization, transferability.

text:
The main idea of this paragraph is an evaluation of using linear interpolation (lerp) to improve the visual smoothness of object movement in a networked game built with Unity, while also addressing its limitations such as jitter and incorrect rendering of teleports. The paragraph introduces an improved synchronization method: buffering all incoming state updates with timestamps, thereby enabling smoother gameplay at the cost of increased processing, and describes how the client processes these buffered snapshots for interpolation, referencing figure 5.2 for illustration.

While employing lerp helps alleviate some of the choppiness in object movement within the Unity-based game, it is insufficient in mitigating jitter and does not accurately represent instantaneous position changes, such as teleports, which instead appear as rapid movements to the player. Previous approaches have attempted to resolve this by including a reset flag with state packets, yet a more effective strategy involves buffering all incoming server updates rather than retaining only the latest state. This approach equips the client with a richer set of data, enabling significantly smoother gameplay, albeit with increased processing demands. Each state update packet is now accompanied by a timestamp indicating when the state was recorded (see figure 5.2). During each iteration of the client game loop, the system reads from this buffer, selecting the most recent snapshot whose timestamp precedes the current reference time to serve as the target for interpolation. This process can involve consuming several snapshots from the buffer. The subsequent step is to apply lerp between the previous interpolation target and the newly selected one, further enhancing synchronization and visual fidelity.

Additionally, these tags utilize an internal power source to energize the integrated circuits within the card. This hybrid functionality enables Semi-Passive RFID Tags to integrate the benefits and constraints associated with both passive and active RFID technologies, as summarized in Table 3.5. The adoption of Semi-Passive RFID Tags in logistics warehouses thus offers a balanced approach, potentially enhancing inventory rotation efficiency while addressing the energy consumption and communication range concerns highlighted in previous studies such as Wang et al. (2019) and Smith (2021). text: Face performance capture and reenactment techniques have traditionally relied on multiple cameras and sensors, often requiring heavy wearable devices or setups positioned at a distance from the subject’s face, thus limiting their practicality in mobile and outdoor environments. EgoFace introduces a novel, lightweight approach to face performance capture and front-view videorealistic reenactment by utilizing a single egocentric RGB camera. This streamlined configuration enables operations in uncontrolled and dynamic settings, making it particularly suited for telepresence applications such as video conferencing on the move. The technique projects input images into a low-dimensional latent space representing facial expression parameters, and, through carefully designed adversarial training in parameter-space synthetic rendering, generates highly realistic facial animations. Addressing the inherent challenges posed by the human visual system’s sensitivity to facial irregularities, especially in video outputs, EgoFace employs a supervised pre-processing training stage that eliminates the need for manual annotations. The system is capable of capturing a broad range of facial expressions, including complex mouth movements and asymmetrical features, and remains robust under varying illumination, backgrounds, and user motion, supporting real-time operation across diverse ethnicities and environments.

text: This paper presents a novel self-supervised approach for estimating optical flow from facial movements, leveraging the inherent structure of human faces to improve flow estimation accuracy. The proposed approach employs a multi-scale strategy to capture both large and small facial movements, resulting in more accurate and detailed flow estimates. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our self-supervised method, outperforming state-of-the-art supervised techniques in terms of flow estimation accuracy and robustness to varying lighting conditions. The key contributions of this research include the development of a self-supervised framework for facial movement-based optical flow estimation, the introduction of a multi-scale feature extraction strategy, and the demonstration of improved performance on benchmark datasets. This work has significant implications for applications in facial analysis, human-computer interaction, and computer vision, with potential uses in fields such as affective computing, facial recognition, and animation. It coincides with the logistic loss applied to the outputs of a neural network, when the softmax is used. , output: Entropy chéo là một hàm mất mát được sử dụng rộng rãi trong các ứng dụng. Nó trùng khớp với tổn thất logistic được áp dụng cho các đầu ra của mạng thần kinh, khi softmax được sử dụng. , and another medical example, input Hypertension is a condition characterized by high blood pressure , output Tăng huyết áp là một tình trạng đặc trưng bởi huyết áp cao . Evidently, Google Translate’s translation proficiency is reduced when handling sentences from such specialized domains. To address this limitation, the proposed methodology involves leveraging existing English-Vietnamese machine translation resources, filtering data relevant to the domain of interest, and applying domain tag control techniques during the NMT training process. In Vietnam, VietAI, a non-profit organization, has explored multi-domain machine translation by creating quality domain-specific datasets and then fine-tuning pre-trained models. Inspired by this approach, the current system utilizes VietAI’s Mtet dataset.

text: This paper is motivated by the need for an efficient approach to generate novel multi-element stable chemical compounds for real-world applications, addressing the combinatorial challenge and extensive expert time required for construction and evaluation of new materials. The authors propose leveraging unsupervised learning, specifically Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which have shown promise in image processing, though existing cross-domain GANs are insufficient for the higher-order complexity in materials science. To address this gap, the paper introduces CrystalGAN, a novel GAN architecture designed to generate chemically stable crystallographic structures with increased domain complexity. The approach includes a new architecture and corresponding loss functions, demonstrating that CrystalGAN produces reasonable and effective data. The method's efficiency is illustrated on the problem of discovering novel hydrides for hydrogen storage, with implications for accelerating materials discovery and inspiring future research into machine learning-driven synthesis of complex compounds. text: This article surveys the intricate connections between Machine Learning (ML) and Control Theory. Control Theory provides a foundational framework, offering valuable concepts and tools for various ML applications. Conversely, ML offers powerful methodologies to address complex and large-scale control problems. The paper is structured into five main parts. The first part explores the synergistic relationship between reinforcement learning and Markov Decision Processes, which are fundamental to discrete-time control problems. The second part examines supervised learning, detailing its relationship with static optimization; within this context, deep learning, an extension of supervised learning, is also conceptualized as a control problem. The third part delves into the theoretical links between stochastic gradient descent and mean-field theory. Finally, the fourth and fifth parts shift focus to Machine Learning approaches for stochastic control problems, with a particular emphasis on the deterministic case to facilitate a clearer exposition of the underlying numerical algorithms.

text: Recent advances in semi-supervised learning have demonstrated significant progress in utilizing both labeled and unlabeled data, though most approaches assume models are randomly initialized. In this study, we integrate semi-supervised learning with transfer learning to establish a more practical and effective framework that leverages both powerful pre-trained models from a source domain and labeled/unlabeled data from a target domain. To maximize the benefits of pre-trained weights and unlabeled target samples, we propose an adaptive consistency regularization comprising two complementary components: Adaptive Knowledge Consistency (AKC), which aligns examples between the source and target models, and Adaptive Representation Consistency (ARC), which aligns representations within the target model between labeled and unlabeled examples. The examples used for consistency regularization are adaptively chosen based on their potential relevance to the target task. We perform extensive evaluations on standard benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CUB-200, and MURA by fine-tuning an ImageNet pre-trained ResNet-50 model. Our results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive consistency regularization surpasses leading semi-supervised learning methods such as Pseudo Label, Mean Teacher, and FixMatch. Furthermore, since our approach is complementary to existing techniques, it achieves additional improvements when combined with MixMatch and FixMatch. The code for our method is available at https://github.com/SHI-Labs/Semi-Supervised-Transfer-Learning.

This paper investigates the "gradient descent" approach to GAN optimization, specifically the natural setting where minor gradient adjustments are concurrently applied to both generator and discriminator parameters. We demonstrate that, despite GAN optimization not corresponding to a convex-concave game (even with basic parameterizations), its equilibrium points can still be valid for the traditional GAN formulation under specific conditions. Conversely, our findings indicate that the more recent Wasserstein GAN can exhibit non-convergent limit cycles close to its equilibrium. Inspired by this stability analysis, we introduce an additional regularization term for gradient descent GAN updates. This term is capable of ensuring local stability for both the WGAN and traditional GAN, and also demonstrates practical potential for accelerating convergence and mitigating mode collapse.

text: Sampling patterns in point cloud Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) significantly influence generation quality, an aspect often overlooked in current research. Investigations reveal that discriminators exhibit varying sensitivities to these patterns, directly impacting the fidelity of generated shapes. Specifically, sampling-insensitive discriminators frequently yield shape point clouds plagued by point clustering artifacts, while excessively sampling-oversensitive counterparts hinder valid shape generation altogether. The concept of a "sampling spectrum" effectively characterizes these diverse discriminator sensitivities. Furthermore, different evaluation metrics weigh sampling patterns against geometric accuracy distinctively, leading to the development of novel perceptual metrics that also span a sampling spectrum. Guided by these insights, a novel middle-point sampling-aware baseline discriminator, PointNet-Mix, was identified. This discriminator substantially enhances the performance of existing point cloud generators across sampling-related metrics, suggesting that the primary bottleneck in point cloud GANs lies not in generator advancements, but rather in the sophisticated design of discriminators. This comprehensive understanding provides critical guidance and practical tools for future discriminator development.

text: In this work, we first describe a framework for the application of Reinforcement Learning (RL) control to a radar system that operates in a congested spectral setting. Each RL technique is evaluated in terms of convergence, radar detection performance achieved in a congested spectral environment, and the ability to share 100MHz spectrum with an uncooperative communications system. We examine policy iteration, which solves an environment posed as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) by directly solving for a stochastic mapping between environmental states and radar waveforms, as well as Deep RL techniques, which utilize a form of Q-Learning to approximate a parameterized function that is used by the radar to select optimal actions. We show that RL techniques are beneficial over a Sense-and-Avoid (SAA) scheme and discuss the conditions under which each approach is most effective.

Sự khác biệt cá nhân này dẫn đến việc hình thành các tập luật không đồng nhất cho cùng một vấn đề, dù về lý thuyết có thể đạt được kết quả tương tự nhưng về cấu trúc nội tại và logic triển khai lại có sự sai khác đáng kể. Điều này không chỉ gây khó khăn trong việc đánh giá và so sánh hiệu suất giữa các hệ thống được phát triển bởi các cá nhân hoặc nhóm khác nhau mà còn làm tăng tính chủ quan của hệ thống, khi mà các quyết định đưa ra có thể bị ảnh hưởng bởi thiên kiến của người thiết kế luật ban đầu. Hơn nữa, quá trình chuyển đổi tri thức tiềm ẩn từ kinh nghiệm của chuyên gia thành các quy tắc tường minh là một thách thức lớn, thường được gọi là "nút cổ chai thu nhận tri thức" (knowledge acquisition bottleneck). Các chuyên gia có thể khó khăn trong việc diễn đạt chính xác toàn bộ quá trình suy luận của họ, dẫn đến việc bỏ sót các trường hợp biên quan trọng hoặc tạo ra các quy tắc mơ hồ, không đầy đủ. Khi hệ thống ngày càng phức tạp và đòi hỏi số lượng luật lớn hơn để bao quát mọi tình huống, việc duy trì, cập nhật và mở rộng tập luật trở thành một gánh nặng khổng lồ. Đặc biệt, nếu người tạo luật ban đầu không còn tham gia vào dự án, việc giải mã và thích nghi với "cách viết" riêng của họ để sửa đổi hoặc bổ sung luật có thể tốn rất nhiều thời gian và nguồn lực. Điều này làm suy giảm đáng kể tính bền vững và khả năng hợp tác trong quá trình phát triển và vận hành hệ thống. Mặt khác, các hệ thống dựa trên luật có xu hướng thiếu tính linh hoạt và khả năng tổng quát hóa. Chúng hoạt động hiệu quả nhất trong các kịch bản đã được định nghĩa rõ ràng và mã hóa thành luật, nhưng lại dễ dàng thất bại (tức là "dễ vỡ" - brittle) khi gặp phải các tình huống mới, chưa từng được dự đoán hoặc các ngoại lệ. Điều này đòi hỏi sự can thiệp thủ công liên tục để cập nhật tập luật mỗi khi có yêu cầu mới hoặc dữ liệu mới xuất hiện, làm tăng chi phí vận hành và làm chậm quá trình thích ứng của hệ thống với môi trường thay đổi. So với các phương pháp học máy dựa trên dữ liệu, hệ thống luật không có khả năng tự học hoặc tự điều chỉnh từ dữ liệu mới mà không cần lập trình lại. Sự cứng nhắc trong cấu trúc luật làm cho chúng không thể tự động khám phá các mối quan hệ ẩn sâu hoặc tự cải thiện hiệu suất theo thời gian. Tính mạnh mẽ của hệ thống phụ thuộc hoàn toàn vào sự đầy đủ và chính xác của từng luật do chuyên gia định nghĩa. The main idea of the paragraph is the introduction and explanation of the strategies used in this thesis to enhance domain adaptive semantic segmentation performance. Specifically, it discusses the incorporation of prototypes at the output level alongside feature-level adaptation, the proposal of two prototype updating methods, and two contrastive loss computation techniques using pseudo labels. The paragraph also introduces a novel mixing technique to address dataset imbalance by targeting rare classes rather than employing random pixel selection. The method is shown to improve performance for challenging classes, though the "train" class remains problematic, indicating that further information alone is insufficient for this class. A seminal work by J. Long, E. Shelhamer, and T. Darrell (2015) is cited as related research.

To further enhance adaptation performance in domain adaptive semantic segmentation, prototypes at the output level are employed in conjunction with feature-level adaptation. This thesis presents two distinct strategies for updating these prototypes, as well as two approaches for calculating contrastive loss based on generated pseudo labels. Moreover, a novel mixing technique is proposed to effectively mitigate dataset imbalance; unlike previous methods that randomly copy and paste pixels, the new approach deliberately selects regions containing pixels from rare classes. This targeted strategy enables the model to access more information regarding difficult classes, resulting in significant performance improvements for those categories. However, the persistent underperformance of the "train" class suggests that simply augmenting class information is not a comprehensive solution for all categories. The methods developed in this thesis build upon foundational work such as that of J. Long, E. Shelhamer, and T. Darrell, “Fully convolutional networks for semantic segmentation,” in Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition, 2015, pp. 3431–3440, while introducing novel contributions in prototype management and data mixing for improved domain adaptation.

text:
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various domains, yet their training dynamics remain a critical area of research. This paper addresses the challenge of improving training efficiency and stability by introducing a novel approach called *Controllable Orthogonalization*. The proposed method dynamically enforces orthogonality constraints on the weight matrices during training, aiming to mitigate issues such as vanishing gradients, poor conditioning, and overfitting. We present a lightweight, computationally efficient algorithm that integrates seamlessly into existing optimization frameworks, such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and its variants. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances convergence speed and model generalization compared to traditional training methods. Furthermore, the method exhibits robustness across diverse architectures, including convolutional and recurrent neural networks. The findings suggest that controllable orthogonalization offers a promising direction for improving the scalability and reliability of DNN training, with potential applications in large-scale AI systems and resource-constrained environments.  

**Keywords**: Deep Neural Networks, Orthogonalization, Training Dynamics, Optimization, Gradient Descent, Model Generalization.

Trong bối cảnh an ninh ứng dụng web, một lỗ hổng phổ biến là khả năng người dùng đã xác thực khai thác các điểm yếu trong kiểm soát truy cập để truy cập trái phép vào thông tin hoặc tài nguyên của người dùng khác. Hiện tượng này thường xảy ra khi người dùng chủ động sửa đổi các tham số trong URL (Uniform Resource Locator) hoặc dữ liệu gửi kèm theo yêu cầu HTTP, chẳng hạn như ID đối tượng hoặc mã định danh tài khoản, nhằm vượt qua các giới hạn quyền truy cập do hệ thống đặt ra (OWASP, 2021; Smith & Johnson, 2019). text: In recent years, deep neural networks have been effectively utilized in reinforcement learning domains \cite. Deep reinforcement learning \cite has demonstrated the benefit of learning robust policies directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs, surpassing traditional agents. Despite these advances, the current literature lacks fundamental changes or improvements to the prevailing training frameworks. In this work, we introduce a novel training framework that is both conceptually straightforward and potentially adaptable to a wide range of reinforcement learning algorithms. Our approach leverages Monte-Carlo sampling to obtain raw data inputs, which are then trained in batches to form Markov decision process sequences, with synchronous updates to network parameters replacing the use of experience replay. This framework enables optimization of an unbiased loss function approximation, ensuring that the estimation precisely aligns with the true probability distribution of the data inputs, resulting in significant enhancements in sample efficiency and convergence rate compared to existing deep reinforcement learning methods, as demonstrated on both discrete action spaces and continuous control tasks. Additionally, we present several algorithms incorporating our new framework to address standard discrete and continuous scenarios. These algorithms exhibit substantially greater efficiency than their original counterparts within the deep reinforcement learning framework and offer practical examples for both current and future algorithms to be extended to our approach.

text: Contrastive learning has demonstrated promising performance across various downstream tasks, often rivaling that of supervised learning. This framework is applicable in both supervised and unsupervised contexts. In the absence of labels, models consider random samples from the same data batch as negative samples while augmenting positive ones, a setting known as self-supervised learning. Conversely, when labels are available, similar samples belong to the same class, while dissimilar samples come from different classes. Supervised contrastive learning has garnered significant attention due to its advantages in representation learning. Research verifies that supervised contrastive loss produces learned representations that are more stable in response to hyperparameter variations. In a recent study, it is shown that integrating supervised contrastive loss with cross-entropy loss enhances the robustness of pre-trained language models against varying noise levels and improves their ability to generalize to related downstream tasks with limited labeled data. Aligning with these studies, my thesis combines both objective functions; however, I observed suboptimal results in the context of continual learning. Consequently, I conducted an analysis to gain a deeper understanding of this outcome.

This paper introduces *img2pose*, a novel framework for simultaneous face alignment and detection using 6 Degrees of Freedom (6DoF) face pose estimation. Traditional methods often treat face detection and alignment as separate tasks, leading to inefficiencies and suboptimal performance. *img2pose* addresses this limitation by directly estimating the 3D pose of a face in an image, enabling precise localization and alignment in a unified approach. The proposed method leverages a deep neural network architecture trained to predict the 6DoF pose parameters (translation and rotation) of a face relative to the camera. By incorporating 3D facial landmarks and pose information, *img2pose* achieves robust performance across varying head poses, lighting conditions, and occlusions. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both face detection and alignment tasks, particularly in challenging scenarios such as extreme angles and partial occlusions. The approach also shows significant improvements in computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications. The key contributions of this work include a unified framework for face detection and alignment, a novel 6DoF pose estimation model, and a robust solution for handling diverse real-world conditions. *img2pose* has potential applications in augmented reality, facial recognition, and human-computer interaction, where accurate and efficient face pose estimation is critical.  

**Keywords**: Face detection, face alignment, 6DoF pose estimation, 3D facial landmarks, deep learning, real-time applications.
label: deepseek-text

text: Vision-based depth estimation is a key feature in autonomous systems, which often relies on a single camera or several independent ones. In such a monocular setup, dense depth is obtained with either additional input from one or several expensive LiDARs, e.g., with 64 beams, or camera-only methods, which suffer from scale-ambiguity and infinite-depth problems. In this paper, we propose a new alternative of densely estimating metric depth by combining a monocular camera with a light-weight LiDAR, e.g., with 4 beams, typical of today's automotive-grade mass-produced laser scanners. Inspired by recent self-supervised methods, we introduce a novel framework, called LiDARTouch, to estimate dense depth maps from monocular images with the help of ``touches'' of LiDAR, i.e., without the need for dense ground-truth depth. In our setup, the minimal LiDAR input contributes on three different levels: as an additional model's input, in a self-supervised LiDAR reconstruction objective function, and to estimate changes of pose (a key component of self-supervised depth estimation architectures). Our LiDARTouch framework achieves new state of the art in self-supervised depth estimation on the KITTI dataset, thus supporting our choices of integrating the very sparse LiDAR signal with other visual features. Moreover, we show that the use of a few-beam LiDAR alleviates scale ambiguity and infinite-depth issues that camera-only methods suffer from. We also demonstrate that methods from the fully-supervised depth-completion literature can be adapted to a self-supervised regime with a minimal LiDAR signal.

text: Unified, real time object detection,” in Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition , 2016, pp. 779–788. This seminal work introduced You Only Look Once (YOLO), a groundbreaking approach that redefined real-time object detection by framing it as a regression problem. Unlike previous two-stage detectors that relied on separate region proposal and classification steps, YOLO employed a single convolutional neural network to predict bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in a single forward pass. The core innovation involved dividing the input image into an S x S grid, where each cell is responsible for predicting B bounding boxes, their confidence scores, and C conditional class probabilities if an object's center falls within that cell. This unified architecture dramatically improved inference speed, enabling real-time performance on high-resolution images, a critical advancement for applications requiring instantaneous detection such as autonomous driving and video surveillance. While initial iterations might have slightly lower localization accuracy compared to slower, two-stage methods for small objects or densely packed scenes, its unparalleled speed and end-to-end training paradigm established a new benchmark and fundamentally influenced the development of subsequent single-shot object detection models, making it a cornerstone for modern computer vision research and practical deployments.

As a demonstrative case, the paper presents ANM6-Easy, an environment specifically designed to encapsulate typical ANM challenges, enabling researchers to benchmark and test RL algorithms effectively. The results highlight Gym-ANM’s potential to accelerate progress in both scientific research and educational settings by lowering barriers to entry and fostering reproducibility. The authors conclude by emphasizing the anticipated role of Gym-ANM in bridging the gap between the power system and RL communities, ultimately supporting the development of advanced algorithms for future energy systems and suggesting directions for future research in collaborative and interdisciplinary domains. text: We present an extension to the model-free anomaly detection algorithm, Isolation Forest. This extension, named Extended Isolation Forest (EIF), resolves issues with assignment of anomaly score to given data points. We motivate the problem using heat maps for anomaly scores. These maps suffer from artifacts generated by the criteria for branching operation of the binary tree. We explain this problem in detail and demonstrate the mechanism by which it occurs visually. We then propose two different approaches for improving the situation. First we propose transforming the data randomly before creation of each tree, which results in averaging out the bias. Second, which is the preferred way, is to allow the slicing of the data to use hyperplanes with random slopes. This approach results in remedying the artifact seen in the anomaly score heat maps. We show that the robustness of the algorithm is much improved using this method by looking at the variance of scores of data points distributed along constant level sets. We report AUROC and AUPRC for our synthetic datasets, along with real-world benchmark datasets. We find no appreciable difference in the rate of convergence nor in computation time between the standard Isolation Forest and EIF.

Merge those two clusters This iterative process continues until all the clusters are merged together.Association Association Rule Learning is a rule-based machine learning method for discovering interesting relations between variables in large databases. It is intended to identify strong rules discovered in databases using some measures of interestingness. In any given transaction with a variety of items, association rules are meant to discover the rules that determine how or why certain items are connected based on a series of metrics such as, support and confidence. These rules, typically represented in an 'if-then' format (e.g., If A then B), are pivotal for extracting interpretable patterns from complex datasets, quantifying the likelihood of a consequent occurring given an antecedent. In the context of Violence Detection in Surveillance Camera, this method can identify specific sequences of events or co-occurring visual features (e.g., rapid motion, specific body postures, or sudden changes in proximity) that frequently precede or constitute violent incidents. The process generally involves two key phases: first, identifying all frequent itemsets that satisfy a minimum support threshold, and subsequently, generating strong association rules from these frequent itemsets that meet a predefined minimum confidence threshold. While **support** measures the prevalence of an itemset within the entire dataset, indicating how often a particular set of features appears together, **confidence** assesses the reliability of the rule, representing the conditional probability of the consequent appearing given the antecedent. Furthermore, **lift** is another crucial metric, evaluating the strength of association between the antecedent and consequent, relative to what would be expected by chance, with a lift value greater than one suggesting a positive correlation. This rule-based approach empowers surveillance systems to learn and articulate explicit, human-understandable rules, such as "If an individual exhibits sudden erratic movement AND approaches another individual aggressively, THEN there is a high probability of an impending violent act," thereby enhancing the system's predictive capabilities for proactive intervention and real-time alerts.

Scene text detection is a critical task in computer vision, with applications ranging from document analysis to autonomous systems. Despite significant progress, real-time detection of text in complex scenes remains challenging due to variations in text size, orientation, and background clutter. This paper introduces STELA (Scene Text detector with LEarned Anchors), a novel real-time text detection framework designed to address these challenges. STELA leverages a lightweight neural network architecture combined with a dynamic anchor generation mechanism, which adaptively learns optimal anchor configurations for diverse text instances. The proposed approach eliminates the need for manually predefined anchors, enhancing detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including ICDAR2015 and MSRA-TD500, demonstrate that STELA achieves state-of-the-art performance with a detection speed of 45 FPS on a single GPU. Compared to existing methods, STELA improves precision by 3.2% and recall by 2.8% while reducing inference time by 20%. The results highlight the effectiveness of learned anchors in improving text localization and the framework's suitability for real-world applications. This work contributes to advancing real-time scene text detection by offering a robust, efficient, and scalable solution.  

**Keywords**: Scene text detection, real-time systems, learned anchors, computer vision, neural networks.
