text: Cross-pose face recognition remains a significant challenge for deep learning algorithms, primarily due to intra-class discrepancy and pose imbalances in training datasets. To address this, we present a novel method that progressively transforms profile face representations to the canonical pose with an attentive pair-wise loss. Our approach first learns feature residuals block-by-block between source and nearby poses, enabling gradual traversal to smaller pose feature spaces for easier transformation. An attentive pair-wise loss then effectively guides this feature transformation. Our proposed progressive module and attentive pair-wise loss are light-weight and easy to implement, adding only about 7:5% extra parameters. Evaluations on the CFP and CPLFW datasets demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method. This effective and cheap approach provides a robust solution for cross-pose face recognition, holding significant promise for improving performance and enabling practical deployment in various real-world applications.

text: Triplet Loss là một phương pháp mới được áp dụng trong việc học và nhận dạng khuôn mặt, thay thế cho các hàm loss truyền thống. Thay vì chỉ so sánh giá trị đầu ra của mạng với ground truth thực tế của dữ liệu, Triplet Loss đưa ra một công thức mới bao gồm ba giá trị đầu vào: anchor (ảnh đầu ra của mạng), positive (ảnh cùng là một người với anchor) và negative (ảnh không cùng là một người với anchor). Kiến trúc FaceNet, được minh họa ở Hình 3.5, sử dụng mô hình học từ đầu đến cuối, bao gồm việc sử dụng ZDNet hoặc Inception Network làm kiến trúc cơ bản. Để giảm số lượng tham số, mô hình thêm các phép chập 1*1 vào kiến trúc, tạo ra các vectơ nhúng hình ảnh f(x) và thực hiện chuẩn hóa L2 cho những vectơ này. Mục tiêu của hàm mất mát này là tạo ra khoảng cách bình phương nhỏ giữa hai lần nhúng hình ảnh của cùng một danh tính (độ tương đồng) và khoảng cách bình phương lớn giữa hai lần nhúng hình ảnh có danh tính khác nhau (độ khác biệt). FaceNet sử dụng một hàm mất mát mới được gọi là Triplet loss, cho phép mô hình học và duy trì một bên gờ (lề) hiệu quả giữa các khuôn mặt có danh tính khác nhau, đảm bảo việc nhúng gần nhau cho các khuôn mặt cùng một người và tách bệt hơn cho các khuôn mặt khác nhau.

text: USB cho phép kết nối với máy tính, thường dùng nạp mã code từ máy tính sang board mạch Arduino. Vai trò của giao tiếp USB trong hệ sinh thái Arduino vượt xa một kết nối vật lý đơn thuần, nó thiết lập một kênh truyền thông nối tiếp ảo (virtual serial communication port) giữa máy tính chủ và vi điều khiển trên bảng mạch Arduino. Quá trình này được thực hiện thông qua một bộ chuyển đổi USB-to-Serial (USB-to-Serial converter), thường là các chip chuyên dụng như FTDI FT232RL, CH340G, hoặc vi điều khiển ATmega16U2/ATmega32U4 được cấu hình để hoạt động như một cầu nối UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) trên các bảng Arduino chính thức. Bộ chuyển đổi này có nhiệm vụ phiên dịch giao thức USB từ phía máy tính thành giao thức nối tiếp UART mà vi điều khiển chính (ví dụ: ATmega328P, ESP32) có thể hiểu và xử lý. Khi người dùng thực hiện thao tác nạp mã code (upload sketch) từ môi trường phát triển tích hợp Arduino IDE, mã nguồn đã được biên dịch thành mã nhị phân (thường dưới dạng tệp .hex) sẽ được truyền tải qua cổng nối tiếp ảo này. Trên bảng mạch Arduino, một chương trình nhỏ gọi là bộ nạp khởi động (bootloader) đã được cài đặt sẵn trong một phần bộ nhớ flash được bảo vệ. Bộ nạp khởi động này có chức năng lắng nghe trên cổng nối tiếp UART để nhận mã chương trình mới. Khi nhận được mã, nó sẽ ghi (flash) dữ liệu này vào bộ nhớ chương trình chính của vi điều khiển. Sau khi quá trình ghi hoàn tất, bộ nạp khởi động sẽ tự động chuyển quyền điều khiển cho chương trình mới được nạp, cho phép chương trình đó bắt đầu thực thi. Cơ chế này loại bỏ sự cần thiết của các thiết bị lập trình phần cứng phức tạp bên ngoài, giúp quá trình phát triển trở nên đơn giản và thuận tiện. Ngoài chức năng nạp mã, kết nối USB còn đóng vai trò then chốt trong quá trình gỡ lỗi và tương tác thời gian thực thông qua tính năng Serial Monitor của Arduino IDE. Các dữ liệu như giá trị cảm biến, trạng thái hoạt động, hoặc thông báo lỗi từ vi điều khiển có thể được gửi ngược lại máy tính để hiển thị, và ngược lại, máy tính có thể gửi các lệnh điều khiển tới board mạch. Điều này tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho việc kiểm tra, hiệu chỉnh và giám sát hoạt động của hệ thống nhúng trong suốt quá trình phát triển. Hơn nữa, giao diện USB còn là nguồn cấp năng lượng chính cho hầu hết các board mạch Arduino trong giai đoạn phát triển và thử nghiệm, thông qua đường VBUS của chuẩn USB, loại bỏ sự cần thiết của bộ nguồn phụ. Sự phổ biến rộng rãi của cổng USB trên các máy tính hiện đại và khả năng tự động nhận diện thiết bị (plug-and-play) nhờ các trình điều khiển chuẩn hóa đã góp phần đáng kể vào sự dễ dàng tiếp cận và sử dụng của nền tảng Arduino cho cả người mới bắt đầu và các nhà nghiên cứu chuyên nghiệp. Đối với một số board mạch Arduino nâng cao như Arduino Leonardo, Arduino Micro, hoặc Arduino Due, vi điều khiển tích hợp có khả năng giao tiếp USB bản địa (native USB capabilities). Điều này cho phép chúng không chỉ hoạt động như một cổng nối tiếp ảo mà còn có thể giả lập các thiết bị USB khác như bàn phím (keyboard), chuột (mouse) hoặc thậm chí là thiết bị lưu trữ (mass storage device), mở rộng đáng kể phạm vi ứng dụng trong các dự án giao diện người-máy (Human Interface Device - HID) hoặc các hệ thống thu thập dữ liệu chuyên sâu.

text: This study presents a novel approach to reconstructing three-dimensional shapes from two-dimensional line drawings. The proposed technique accepts one or multiple sketches as input and generates a dense point cloud that represents the 3D reconstruction of the input sketch(es), which is subsequently converted into a polygon mesh. A deep encoder-decoder network is the core component of this method, where the encoder extracts a compact representation of the sketch that encapsulates shape information, and the decoder transforms this representation into depth and normal maps that capture the underlying surface from multiple viewpoints. These multi-view maps are then combined into a 3D point cloud by solving an optimization problem that integrates depth and normals across all viewpoints. As demonstrated by our experimental results, our architecture outperforms other methods, such as volumetric networks, in terms of reconstruction fidelity, surface resolution, and preservation of topology and shape structure, as shown in Figure A, B, C (References [citation]).

text: Domain Adaptation (DA) techniques have shown notable success across various machine learning and computer vision tasks, including classification, detection, and segmentation; however, the direct application of DA methods to 3D point cloud data remains underexplored due to the intricate spatial and geometric characteristics inherent to such data. The semantics of 3D objects in point clouds are heavily influenced by regional geometric structures, posing challenges for conventional DA methods that primarily focus on global feature alignment while neglecting critical local geometric information. Addressing this limitation, a novel 3D Domain Adaptation Network (PointDAN) is introduced to facilitate effective domain adaptation for point cloud data through the joint alignment of global and local features at multiple hierarchical levels. The approach incorporates a Self-Adaptive (SA) node module, which employs an adaptive receptive field to capture and align discriminative local structures, and a node-attention mechanism to model relationships among SA nodes, thereby enhancing feature representation across both objects and domains. Global feature alignment is further achieved using an adversarial-training strategy. In the absence of a standardized evaluation framework for 3D point cloud DA, a comprehensive benchmark, PointDA-10, is established using data from ModelNet, ShapeNet, and ScanNet to enable cross-domain object classification. Experimental results on PointDA-10 demonstrate the clear superiority of the proposed model over existing general-purpose DA methods.

text:
Recommender systems play a critical role in personalizing user experiences across digital platforms. However, designing effective input representations for these systems remains a significant challenge, as traditional methods often rely on handcrafted features or predefined embeddings. This paper introduces Differentiable Neural Input Search (DNIS), a novel framework that automates the process of identifying optimal input representations for recommender systems. DNIS leverages differentiable architecture search techniques to dynamically explore and combine diverse feature embeddings, enabling the system to adaptively learn the most informative inputs for recommendation tasks. We evaluate DNIS on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating its ability to outperform state-of-the-art methods in terms of recommendation accuracy and computational efficiency. The results highlight the framework's capability to reduce manual feature engineering efforts while improving model performance. DNIS represents a significant step forward in automating the design of recommender systems, offering a scalable and flexible solution for real-world applications. Key contributions include the integration of differentiable search mechanisms into recommendation pipelines and the demonstration of its effectiveness across diverse datasets. This work opens new avenues for research in automated feature learning and its applications in personalized recommendation systems.  

**Keywords**: Recommender Systems, Differentiable Architecture Search, Neural Input Search, Feature Embeddings, Automated Feature Learning.

text: Recently, unsupervised exemplar-based image-to-image translation, conditioned on a given exemplar without the paired data, has accomplished substantial advancements. In order to transfer the information from an exemplar to an input image, existing methods often use a normalization technique, e.g., adaptive instance normalization, that controls the channel-wise statistics of an input activation map at a particular layer, such as the mean and the variance. Meanwhile, style transfer approaches similar task to image translation by nature, demonstrated superior performance by using the higher-order statistics such as covariance among channels in representing a style. In detail, it works via whitening (given a zero-mean input feature, transforming its covariance matrix into the identity). followed by coloring (changing the covariance matrix of the whitened feature to those of the style feature). However, applying this approach in image translation is computationally intensive and error-prone due to the expensive time complexity and its non-trivial backpropagation. In response, this paper proposes an end-to-end approach tailored for image translation that efficiently approximates this transformation with our novel regularization methods. We further extend our approach to a group-wise form for memory and time efficiency as well as image quality. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that our proposed method is fast, both in training and inference, and highly effective in reflecting the style of an exemplar. Finally, our code is available at https://github.com/WonwoongCho/GDWCT.

text: In this paper, we demonstrate that Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are prone to catastrophic forgetting, even when trained to approximate a single target distribution. We establish that GAN training constitutes a continual learning problem, wherein the sequence of evolving model distributions serves as a sequence of tasks for the discriminator. The degree of mismatch between these tasks dictates the extent of forgetting. Catastrophic forgetting is linked to mode collapse and can result in non-convergent training of GANs. Our investigation into the landscape of the discriminator's output across various GAN variants reveals that, upon convergence to a favorable equilibrium, real training datapoints become wide local maxima of the discriminator. We empirically explore the connection between the sharpness of these local maxima and both mode collapse and generalization in GANs. Furthermore, we illustrate how catastrophic forgetting hinders the discriminator from rendering real datapoints as local maxima, thereby leading to non-convergence. Lastly, we examine strategies to prevent catastrophic forgetting in GANs.

text: Recently there has been increased interest in semi-supervised classification in the presence of graphical information. A new class of learning models has emerged that relies, at its most basic level, on classifying the data after first applying a graph convolution. To understand the merits of this approach, we study the classification of a mixture of Gaussians, where the data corresponds to the node attributes of a stochastic block model. We show that graph convolution extends the regime in which the data is linearly separable by a factor of roughly 1/, where D is the expected degree of a node, as compared to the mixture model data on its own. Furthermore, we find that the linear classifier obtained by minimizing the cross-entropy loss after the graph convolution generalizes to out-of-distribution data where the unseen data can have different intra- and inter-class edge probabilities from the training data.

text: This paper presents a technique for reduced-order Markov modeling for compact representation of time-series data. In this work, symbolic dynamics-based tools have been used to infer an approximate generative Markov model. The time-series data are first symbolized by partitioning the continuous measurement space of the signal and then, the discrete sequential data are modeled using symbolic dynamics. In the proposed approach, the size of temporal memory of the symbol sequence is estimated from spectral properties of the resulting stochastic matrix corresponding to a first-order Markov model of the symbol sequence. Then, hierarchical clustering is used to represent the states of the corresponding full-state Markov model to construct a reduced-order or size Markov model with a non-deterministic algebraic structure. Subsequently, the parameters of the reduced-order Markov model are identified from the original model by making use of a Bayesian inference rule. The final model is selected using information-theoretic criteria. The proposed concept is elucidated and validated on two different data sets as examples. The first example analyzes a set of pressure data from a swirl-stabilized combustor, where controlled protocols are used to induce flame instabilities. Variations in the complexity of the derived Markov model represent how the system operating condition changes from a stable to an unstable combustion regime. In the second example, the data set is taken from NASA's data repository for prognostics of bearings on rotating shafts. We show that, even with a very small state-space, the reduced-order models are able to achieve comparable performance and that the proposed approach provides flexibility in the selection of a final model for representation and learning.

text: This paper proposes a novel approach to learning disentangled representations by leveraging the concept of product manifold projection. The objective is to develop a framework that can effectively separate the factors of variation in complex data, enabling improved interpretability and generalizability of machine learning models. Our method utilizes a geometric approach, projecting data onto a product manifold to disentangle the underlying factors. We employ a deep learning architecture to learn the product manifold and a projection operator that maps the data to the disentangled representation. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in learning disentangled representations, outperforming existing methods on several benchmark datasets. The key findings highlight the importance of geometric constraints in disentanglement learning and the potential applications of our method in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and generative modeling. Our research contributes to the development of more interpretable and robust machine learning models, with implications for improved performance and reliability in real-world applications. Key keywords: disentangled representations, product manifold projection, deep learning, geometric methods, interpretability.

The high dimensionality and non-Euclidean nature of these networks pose challenges in depicting their population distribution and correlating them with human traits. Existing methodologies often summarize the network using predetermined topological features or principal components analysis (PCA). In this study, we leverage recent developments in deep learning to propose a nonlinear latent factor model for characterizing the population distribution of brain graphs and elucidating the relationships between brain structural connectomes and human traits, termed Graph AuTo-Encoding (GATE). We applied GATE to two extensive brain imaging datasets—the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study and the Human Connectome Project (HCP) for adults—to investigate the structural brain connectome and its cognitive correlations. Our numerical results indicate that GATE significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy, statistical inference, and computational efficiency. Notably, our findings reveal a stronger association between structural connectomes and a broad spectrum of human cognitive traits than previously identified.

text: 3D morphable models are crucial for representing object class shapes in computer vision and graphics, with recent deep learning approaches operating directly on hierarchical 3D mesh data to capture multi-scale information. This paper investigates the challenge of feature aggregation across hierarchical levels in such models, an area less explored compared to convolution operator design. We introduce an attention-based module that learns mapping matrices for improved vertex feature aggregation, replacing conventional mesh decimation methods. These mapping matrices are generated via a compatibility function between trainable keys and queries, which are shared across all samples of a given object class and optimized with the main objective. Our module serves as a train-only, drop-in replacement for both downsampling and upsampling feature aggregation in existing architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that our end-to-end trainable mapping matrices yield state-of-the-art performance on multiple 3D shape datasets, surpassing existing 3D morphable models.

text: The World Wide Web Consortium - W3C defines an Application Programming Interface (API), as illustrated in Figure 3.4, which depicts how the API functions. Specifically, a, Rest API, also known as a RESTful API, is an application programming interface that strictly adheres to the architectural standards and limitations of REpresentational State Transfer (REST), an architectural style developed by computer scientist Roy Fielding, which is particularly well-suited for scalable, distributed systems like a SaaS-based search engine. These fundamental architectural constraints include client-server separation, ensuring that the client (e.g., a web browser or mobile application) and the server (where the e-commerce data and search logic reside) can evolve independently, thereby promoting flexibility and maintainability. A critical characteristic is statelessness, meaning each request from the client to the server must contain all information necessary to understand and process the request, with the server storing no client context between requests, which significantly enhances scalability and reliability by removing server-side session dependencies. Furthermore, REST APIs mandate a uniform interface, simplifying interactions through standardized methods like HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) for manipulating resources, leading to improved visibility and understandability of the API. Responses from REST APIs are often designed to be cacheable, allowing clients to store past responses and reuse them for future requests, thereby reducing network latency and server load, which is crucial for high-traffic e-commerce sites. The system can also be layered, enabling intermediate servers to enhance scalability, security, or load balancing without affecting the client-server interaction directly. The acronym REST stands for REpresentational State Transfer, and the core idea behind this is the transfer of resource representations (e.g., data in JSON or XML format) between the client and server, with the client receiving a representation of a resource's state and subsequently deciding how to transition to another state, making it an efficient and robust paradigm for client-server communication.

text: Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) task refers to learn a mapping from low-resolution images to the corresponding high-resolution ones. This task is known to be extremely difficult since it is an ill-posed problem. Recently, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved state of the art performance on SISR. However, the images produced by CNNs do not contain fine details of the images. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) aim to solve this issue and recover sharp details. Nevertheless, GANs are notoriously difficult to train. Besides that, they generate artifacts in the high-resolution images. In this paper, we have proposed a method in which CNNs try to align images in different spaces rather than only the pixel space. Such a space is designed using convex optimization techniques. CNNs are encouraged to learn high-frequency components of the images as well as low-frequency components. We have shown that the proposed method can recover fine details of the images and it is stable in the training process.

text: Goal-oriented dialog, a pivotal AI application, involves a questioner seeking a correct action from an answerer. While deep learning and reinforcement learning have been applied to generate effective questions, these methods struggle to develop competent recurrent neural questioners due to the complexity of learning sequential sentences. Motivated by Theory of Mind, we propose "Answerer in Questioner's Mind" (AQM), a novel information-theoretic algorithm for goal-oriented dialog. AQM allows a questioner to infer the answerer's intention via an approximated probabilistic model, explicitly selecting questions by calculating the information gain from candidate intentions and possible answers. Evaluated on "MNIST Counting Dialog" and "GuessWhat?!"—two goal-oriented visual dialog tasks—AQM significantly outperforms comparative algorithms.

The longest life cycle duration (34.7 days) was observed when larvae fed on turmeric leaves, while the shortest (24.2 days) occurred on amaranth leaves. The host plant did not affect the survival rate of eggs and pupae but had a significant effect on larval survival rates. Larval survival was highest (87.6%) on amaranth leaves and lowest (50.0%) on turmeric leaves. The proportion of females at the adult stage was 36.1% when larvae fed on turmeric leaves and 46.7% when fed on chive leaves. Fecundity of adults reached 174.3 and 453.8 eggs/female, respectively, when larvae fed on turmeric and amaranth leaves. text: The rest of my thesis is organized as follows. Chapter 2 provides the literature review for my research. First, I show the scope of my research. After that, I will give the overviews for both Relation Extraction and Continual Learning by giving their definitions, some real-life use cases, and the obstacles to the problems. Relation Extraction (RE) is a fundamental task in natural language processing that focuses on identifying semantic relationships between entities within text, playing a crucial role in knowledge base construction, question answering, and information retrieval. Continual Learning (CL), on the other hand, addresses the challenge of enabling models to learn new information incrementally without forgetting previously acquired knowledge, which is vital for adapting to dynamic data environments and real-world applications where data evolves over time. The intersection of these fields leads to the continual relation extraction problem, which aims to maintain and update relation extraction capabilities as new relation types or data emerge without catastrophic forgetting. Moreover, I will introduce existing continual relation extraction methods such as Experience Replay, Contrastive Replay, and others, discussing their strengths and weaknesses. Experience Replay involves storing and replaying previous samples to mitigate forgetting but may suffer from memory constraints and sampling biases. Contrastive Replay enhances representation learning by contrasting current and past data, improving robustness but requiring careful tuning of contrastive objectives. By analyzing these methods, the chapter sets the foundation for understanding how feature decorrelation techniques can be leveraged to improve continual relation extraction models, ultimately contributing novel insights and methodologies to the field.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of learning disentangled representations in high-dimensional data, a critical task for improving interpretability and generalization in machine learning models. We propose a novel approach based on product manifold projection, which leverages the geometric structure of data to separate underlying factors of variation. Our method projects data onto a product of lower-dimensional manifolds, each corresponding to a distinct latent factor, enabling the model to capture independent and meaningful representations. The approach is implemented using a combination of deep neural networks and manifold optimization techniques, ensuring scalability and efficiency. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing disentanglement techniques in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and disentanglement metrics. Furthermore, the learned representations exhibit improved robustness and transferability across downstream tasks. This work contributes a new perspective on disentanglement by integrating geometric principles with deep learning, offering potential applications in domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, and generative modeling. Our method leverages a spatial attention mechanism to focus on detailed regions and a temporal module to maintain coherence across frames. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of spatial resolution and temporal stability. Our findings suggest that there is indeed a tradeoff between spatial and temporal aspects, and optimizing for one aspect can compromise the other. We conclude that a balanced approach, considering both spatial and temporal factors, is essential for achieving optimal video super-resolution performance. text: Image interpolation, or image morphing, refers to a visual transition between two (or more) input images. For such a transition to look visually appealing, its desirable properties are (i) to be smooth; (ii) to apply the minimal required change in the image; and (iii) to seem "real", avoiding unnatural artifacts in each image in the transition. To obtain a smooth and straightforward transition, one may adopt the well-known Wasserstein Barycenter Problem (WBP). While this approach guarantees minimal changes under the Wasserstein metric, the resulting images might seem unnatural. In this work, we propose a novel approach for image morphing that possesses all three desired properties. To this end, we define a constrained variant of the WBP that enforces the intermediate images to satisfy an image prior. We describe an algorithm that solves this problem and demonstrate it using the sparse prior and generative adversarial networks.

text:
Seed phenotyping is a critical task in agriculture, enabling the assessment of seed quality and traits for improved crop yield. Traditional methods often rely on manual inspection or limited datasets, which are time-consuming and lack scalability. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a novel approach that combines domain randomization and transfer learning within a neural network framework. The objective is to enhance the accuracy and robustness of seed phenotyping models, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data.  

The proposed method leverages domain randomization to generate diverse synthetic datasets, simulating various environmental conditions and seed variations. These datasets are used to pre-train a deep neural network, which is then fine-tuned using transfer learning on a smaller, real-world seed dataset. Experiments demonstrate that this approach significantly improves model performance, achieving higher accuracy and generalization compared to traditional methods. Key findings include a 15% increase in classification accuracy and enhanced robustness to variations in lighting, orientation, and seed morphology.  

The study highlights the potential of combining domain randomization and transfer learning for seed phenotyping, offering a scalable and efficient solution for agricultural applications. This research contributes to the advancement of automated phenotyping technologies, with implications for precision agriculture and crop improvement.  

**Keywords**: seed phenotyping, domain randomization, transfer learning, neural networks, precision agriculture, synthetic data.

text: The robustness of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in safety-critical applications, such as autonomous driving, is paramount, particularly concerning unavoidable image corruptions like noise, with a specific focus on dense semantic segmentation. Building upon insights from image classification that suggest enhancing output robustness through increased network bias towards object shapes, a novel training schema is introduced. This method, termed 'Painting-by-Numbers', improves shape bias by alpha-blending portions of real RGB training images with synthetically generated counterparts. These faked images assign each class-label a fixed, randomly chosen color improbable in natural scenes, thereby compelling the network to prioritize shape cues over color or texture. The efficacy of this augmentation technique was rigorously demonstrated using DeepLabv3+ across various network backbones, including MobileNet-V2, ResNets, and Xception, evaluated on the Cityscapes dataset. When assessed against 16 distinct image corruption types, the proposed schema achieved superior performance compared to training with clean data in 74% of configurations, occasionally showing only marginal declines. Notably, for specific corruptions like image noise, significant performance gains of up to 25% were observed.

Learning from limited data in few-shot scenarios suffers from poor generalization, often losing crucial local and contextual information due to global pooling or independent class processing. This paper introduces Sparse Spatial Transformers (SSFormers), a novel Transformer based neural network addressing these challenges. SSFormers first extracts dense local features from multi-scale image patches, preserving rich contextual information. Subsequently, a sparse spatial transformer layer establishes spatial correspondence across the entire support set, effectively identifying and suppressing task-irrelevant features. Finally, an image patch matching module determines query image categories based on refined local representations. Extensive experiments on popular few-shot learning benchmarks demonstrate that SSFormers achieves state-of-the-art performance, offering a robust solution for few-shot learning by selectively focusing on task-relevant information. text: Heterogeneous Domain Adaptation (HDA) addresses transfer learning challenges where source and target domains differ in modalities or feature dimensions, posing difficulties for traditional domain adaptation algorithms that assume a shared feature space. To overcome these limitations and the computational complexity of current state-of-the-art HDA methods, we introduce the Cross-Domain Structure Preserving Projection (CDSPP) algorithm, which extends classic LPP to heterogeneous domains by learning domain-specific projections that map source and target features into a common subspace while preserving class consistency and aligning data distributions. CDSPP offers a simple, deterministic solution via a generalized eigenvalue problem and is naturally suited for supervised HDA, with an extension to semi-supervised scenarios involving unlabeled target samples. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets such as Office-Caltech, Multilingual Reuters Collection, NUS-WIDE-ImageNet, and the newly introduced Office-Home dataset (with a broader class range) demonstrate that CDSPP consistently outperforms contemporary methods in both supervised and semi-supervised settings, indicating its potential as a generalizable and efficient approach for future HDA research. text: This feature is transferable because, without updating the feature extractor, the representation space is separated to some extent, implying that distinct knowledge structures can be maintained for different tasks with minimal interference, thereby facilitating the adaptation of learned representations to novel scenarios. If the feature extractor learns non transferable features in the previous task, these features can be changed considerably to adapt to the current task, as the model's parameters are heavily adjusted to optimize performance on the new data distribution, often leading to the overwriting of prior knowledge. Consequently, old learned features for previous tasks can be forgotten, leading to the performance reduction on those tasks, a critical challenge in continual learning known as catastrophic forgetting, where the acquisition of new skills diminishes or erases proficiency in previously mastered tasks. Theythen hypothesized that learning transferable and diverse representations is an important requirement for incremental learning, as transferable features ensure generalizability across sequential tasks, while diverse features enable the model to capture a broader spectrum of underlying data characteristics, thus promoting robust and persistent knowledge accumulation. And through a spectral analysis, they found that in representation space, spectral components with large eigenvalues are more transferable and less forgettable, suggesting that the most significant and stable directions of data variance in the representation space correspond to features that are inherently robust to modification and crucial for maintaining performance across a continuous stream of learning tasks.

text: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) excel in sample quality but often suffer from mode collapse, whereas Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) effectively cover all modes but yield poorer sample quality. Current hybrid VAE-GAN frameworks, attempting to combine these strengths, exhibit limited success primarily due to the VAE objective's inherent trade-off between data log-likelihood and divergence to the latent prior, alongside instability in the synthetic likelihood ratio term. This paper introduces a novel objective for hybrid VAE-GANs, incorporating a "Best-of-Many-Samples" reconstruction cost and a stable direct estimate of the synthetic likelihood. Our proposed methodology enables the hybrid VAE-GAN framework to achieve high data log-likelihood and low divergence to the latent prior simultaneously. As a key finding, this approach demonstrates significant improvements in both mode coverage and sample quality when compared to existing hybrid VAE-GANs and plain GANs, offering a substantial contribution towards more robust and high-fidelity generative modeling.

text: This study seeks to reconstruct the complete three-dimensional shape of a human from a single image, addressing the limitations of existing vertex-level and parameter regression methods that rely on predefined adjacency matrices to represent positive relationships between nodes, thereby neglecting the complex topological relationships on the surface of the human body. Furthermore, current approaches often struggle with significant performance degradation when confronted with occlusion cases in real-world scenarios due to domain gaps. To overcome these challenges, we introduce the Deep Mesh Relation Capturing Graph Convolution Network (DC-GNet), which incorporates a shape completion task to enhance 3D human shape reconstruction. Our approach involves two key innovations: firstly, an adaptive matrix is proposed to capture both positive and negative relationships between mesh vertices, and secondly, a shape completion task is designed to learn about various types of occlusions. By encoding mesh structures based on subtle relationships between nodes in more distant regions, our method improves performance, particularly in outdoor scenes where occlusions are common. text: This paper proposes an innovative no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) approach, leveraging attention-driven mechanisms to evaluate the perceptual quality of images. The objective is to develop a reliable and efficient method for assessing image quality without requiring reference images. Experimental results demonstrate that our attention-driven NR-IQA approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving high correlation with human subjective scores. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of attention mechanisms in NR-IQA, enabling the model to adaptively weigh the importance of different image regions, and the development of a more robust and generalizable image quality assessment framework. This work has significant implications for various applications, including image and video processing, compression, and transmission. text: Coordinate-based Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) networks, while capable of learning neural implicit representations, generally exhibit suboptimal performance for single-image synthesis applications. In contrast, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are typically employed for various generative tasks in this domain, despite their requirement for larger models. We propose Neural Knitwork, an architecture designed for neural implicit representation learning of natural images, which achieves image synthesis by adversarially optimizing the distribution of image patches and enforcing consistency between their predictions. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first implementation of a coordinate-based MLP specifically tailored for critical synthesis tasks such as image inpainting, super-resolution, and denoising. We demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed technique through training on these three tasks. Our results indicate that modeling natural images using patches, rather than individual pixels, yields higher fidelity outcomes. Furthermore, the Neural Knitwork model requires 80% fewer parameters than comparable CNN-based solutions, while maintaining competitive performance and training efficiency.

3.2 Floyd-Warshall Algorithm

The Floyd-Warshall algorithm, named after Robert Floyd and Stephen Warshall, is designed to find the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in a weighted graph. It was published by Robert Floyd in 1962 and independently by Stephen Warshall in the same year. The algorithm operates by gradually refining an estimate of the shortest path lengths between all vertices in the graph.

text: Efficient warehouse management is essential for businesses to ensure the smooth operation of logistics warehouses, and this involves implementing well-structured processes for arranging and classifying items scientifically within the storage space. Utilizing technology applications, such as RFID (Radio Frequency Identification), plays a pivotal role in supporting and enhancing these management activities. RFID technology allows for automated inventory tracking, which significantly improves the accuracy and speed of inventory monitoring compared to traditional manual methods. By continuously and automatically capturing data on item location, quantity, and movement, RFID systems help maintain real-time visibility of stock conditions, enabling businesses to promptly identify discrepancies or potential issues within the inventory management process. This capability is crucial for maintaining the quality and integrity of goods stored, preventing spoilage or damage, which is especially important in logistics warehouses where items may be subject to various environmental factors. Furthermore, automated inventory rotation facilitated by RFID ensures that items are used or shipped in the correct order, adhering to principles such as FIFO (First In, First Out), thereby reducing waste and optimizing stock turnover. The integration of RFID into warehouse management not only supports the scientific classification and arrangement of items but also fortifies the early detection of process errors, ultimately contributing to more efficient logistics operations and improved overall supply chain performance.

text: A novel approach, 3D-RecGAN++, is introduced for reconstructing complete 3D object structures from a single arbitrary depth view utilizing generative adversarial networks. This method represents a significant advancement over existing techniques, which typically demand multiple views of the same object or reliance on class labels to recover full 3D geometry. Instead, 3D-RecGAN++ directly processes a voxel grid representation of a single depth view as input, capable of generating a complete 3D occupancy grid at a high resolution of 256^3 by effectively recovering occluded and missing regions. Its core principle involves integrating the generative capabilities of autoencoders with the conditional Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework, enabling the inference of accurate and fine-grained 3D structures of objects within high-dimensional voxel space. Extensive empirical validation on large synthetic datasets and real-world Kinect datasets demonstrates that 3D-RecGAN++ substantially outperforms the state of the art in single-view 3D object reconstruction, further showcasing its ability to reconstruct previously unseen types of objects.

text: In the domain of feature extraction and classification, experiments with non-fusion deep learning algorithms on the AICS-Violence dataset indicated that while the 3D DenseNet Lean method achieved high accuracy on the Cam1 test set, its performance significantly decreased on the Cam2 test set. However, preliminary investigations demonstrated that employing visualized optical flow as input for 3D DenseNet Lean led to a remarkable accuracy improvement for the Cam2 test set (from 82.03% to 93.7%), with only a marginal performance decrease on the Cam1 test set. Consequently, a novel method is proposed, integrating visualized optical flow and 3D DenseNet Lean, to achieve superior performance across both test sets. text: Consequently, microservices architectures inherently introduce additional latency and overhead due to inter-service communication traversing network interfaces, necessitating data serialization and deserialization across service boundaries. Conversely, monolithic applications leverage significantly faster in-process communication through direct memory access and function calls, thereby minimizing overhead for internal function interactions. This foundational distinction often mandates careful architectural considerations in microservice design to optimize data locality and minimize frequent, synchronous network calls, which can otherwise lead to performance degradation relative to the direct memory access patterns characteristic of monolithic systems.

This section describes the design and workflow of the Helpdesk ticketing system interface developed using OdooErp, outlining the customer’s ticket creation process, interaction with support agents, and administrative management, including the application of SLA policies. The user interface components, such as the Form view and Chatter, are discussed with reference to Figures 4.22–4.24, illustrating how customers submit tickets, track their progress, and communicate with support staff, while administrators oversee ticket approval, assignment, and SLA compliance.

The Form view, as depicted in Figure 4.22, allows customers to input essential information such as name, email, phone number, job title, and specific details related to the ticket they wish to create. Customers can subsequently monitor the status of their submitted tickets through a dedicated portal, which supports the Chatter feature for real-time communication. This functionality enables users to ask further questions, interact directly with the internal user assigned to their ticket, and upload file attachments, thereby facilitating more efficient resolution by the Support Agent (Figure 4.23). Once a ticket is created, administrative personnel review its details, approve the submission, and assign it to an appropriate support agent for resolution, as shown in Figure 4.24. Furthermore, if the administrator opts to apply a Service Level Agreement (SLA) to a ticket, they must populate relevant fields that align with the SLA’s criteria. The criteria section within the SLA configuration is instrumental in determining the tickets to which the policy applies, while the “Target - Reach Stage” specifies the requisite stage and time frame for compliance with the SLA policy. This workflow not only enhances transparency and accountability in the support process but also leverages OdooErp’s integrated communication and SLA management features, contributing to a more robust and user-friendly helpdesk platform.

text: Self-training has emerged as a prominent technique in Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA), supplanting the traditional method of explicitly aligning source and target domain distributions. This approach involves the iterative creation of pseudo labels, which are then used to retrain the network, facilitating adaptation through a self-paced curriculum learning framework. The generation of pseudo labels can occur either online or offline. Due to the inherent discrepancies between source and target distributions, these pseudo labels often contain noise and must be judiciously selected. Conventionally, pseudo labels are chosen based on a strict confidence threshold; however, high confidence scores do not always equate to accuracy, which can hinder the network's ability to acquire reliable information from the target domain. Relying solely on robust predictions may result in certain pixels being perpetually unlearned throughout the training duration. For example, if the model struggles to accurately predict a particular class, assigning pseudo labels to pixels of that class becomes challenging, potentially leading to insufficient and imbalanced training data.

Tìm hiểu và xây dựng game RPG sử dụng Unity engine là một dự án nghiên cứu nhằm khám phá khả năng của công cụ Unity trong việc tạo ra các trò chơi nhập vai (RPG) đa dạng và thú vị. Dự án này tập trung vào việc phân tích và áp dụng các kỹ thuật thiết kế game, lập trình và xây dựng cơ sở hạ tầng cho một trò chơi RPG hoàn chỉnh.

Bằng cách sử dụng Unity engine, dự án này sẽ khám phá khả năng của công cụ này trong việc tạo ra các nhân vật, hệ thống chiến đấu, và môi trường 3D phong phú. Đồng thời, dự án này cũng sẽ nghiên cứu và áp dụng các kỹ thuật thiết kế game để tạo ra một trải nghiệm chơi game hấp dẫn và thú vị cho người chơi.

Dự án này sẽ bao gồm các bước sau: nghiên cứu và phân tích các công nghệ và kỹ thuật hiện đại trong việc tạo ra trò chơi RPG; thiết kế và xây dựng cơ sở hạ tầng cho trò chơi; lập trình và tích hợp các tính năng và hệ thống cho trò chơi; và cuối cùng là thử nghiệm và đánh giá trò chơi.

Mục tiêu của dự án này là tạo ra một trò chơi RPG hoàn chỉnh và đa dạng, sử dụng Unity engine như một công cụ chính để xây dựng và phát triển trò chơi. Dự án này sẽ cung cấp một cái nhìn sâu sắc về khả năng của Unity engine trong việc tạo ra các trò chơi nhập vai và sẽ là một nguồn tham khảo quan trọng cho các nhà phát triển game trong tương lai.

text: Trước nhu cầu phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ ngày càng tăng tại Việt Nam, nghiên cứu này nhằm đánh giá tỷ lệ các loại phẫu thuật phổ biến và phân tích các yếu tố liên quan đến quyết định phẫu thuật của bệnh nhân. Chúng tôi đã thực hiện một nghiên cứu hồi cứu trên 1676 bệnh nhân tại hai cơ sở thẩm mỹ ở TP.HCM, thu thập dữ liệu nhân khẩu học, tiền sử phẫu thuật và các loại hình phẫu thuật, sử dụng phân tích hồi quy đơn biến và đa biến để xác định các yếu tố liên quan. Kết quả cho thấy phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ mắt (79,7%) và mũi (20,9%) là các loại hình phổ biến nhất, với đa số bệnh nhân trên 19 tuổi. Đặc biệt, nhóm bệnh nhân từ 19-34 tuổi và nhóm lớn tuổi có khả năng phẫu thuật cao hơn lần lượt 5 và 3 lần so với nhóm dưới 19 tuổi (p < 0,05), đồng thời nhu cầu tư vấn thẩm mỹ mắt cũng cao hơn khoảng 2 lần (p < 0,05). Phân tích hồi quy đa biến xác nhận tuổi là một yếu tố quan trọng liên quan đến quyết định phẫu thuật. text: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning hyper-heuristic approach for multi-objective single point search, with a specific application to structural fault identification. The proposed approach is evaluated on a set of benchmark problems and a real-world structural fault identification problem, demonstrating its ability to outperform existing methods in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The results show that the reinforcement learning hyper-heuristic can efficiently identify structural faults and provide valuable insights for maintenance and repair operations. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective multi-objective optimization methods, with potential applications in various fields such as engineering, finance, and logistics. text: We present a methodology for parallel acceleration of learning in the presence of matrix orthogonality and unitarity constraints of interest in several branches of machine learning. We show how an apparently sequential elementary rotation parametrization can be restructured into blocks of commutative operations using a well-known tool for coloring the edges of complete graphs, in turn widely applied to schedule round-robin (all-against-all) sports tournaments. The resulting decomposition admits an algorithm to compute a fully-parametrized orthogonal matrix from its rotation parameters in O(n) sequential steps and one to compute the gradient of a training loss with respect to its parameters in O(n\log n) steps. We discuss parametric restrictions of interest to generative modeling and present promising performance results with a prototype GPU implementation. This work motivates further research into efficient parallelization of matrix constraints in deep learning and suggests the potential for broader adoption of such block-structured approaches in generative modeling and related fields.

text: Many time series originate from a combination of deterministic continuous flows and discrete jumps triggered by stochastic events. However, the equation of motion describing these flows, or their interaction with jumps, is typically unknown. To address this challenge, we introduce Neural Jump Stochastic Differential Equations, which offer a data-driven method for learning both continuous and discrete dynamic behavior in hybrid systems that encompass both flowing and jumping characteristics. Our approach extends the framework of Neural Ordinary Differential Equations by incorporating a stochastic process term designed to model discrete events. Subsequently, we model temporal point processes using a piecewise-continuous latent trajectory, where discontinuities arise from stochastic events whose conditional intensity depends on the latent state. We demonstrate the predictive capabilities of our model on various synthetic and real-world marked point process datasets, including classical point processes (such as Hawkes processes), awards on Stack Overflow, medical records, and earthquake monitoring.

text: Safe exploration is crucial for the real-world application of reinforcement learning (RL). Previous works formulate the safe exploration problem as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP), where policies are optimized under specified constraints. However, human learning often prioritizes immediate termination of potentially dangerous situations rather than learning safe behavior within those dangers. Motivated by this human safety principle, we introduce a novel approach to safe RL problems, framed as an Early Terminated MDP (ET-MDP). We define the ET-MDP as an unconstrained Markov Decision Process (MDP) that yields an equivalent optimal value function to its corresponding CMDP. An off-policy algorithm based on context models is subsequently proposed to solve the ET-MDP, thereby addressing the corresponding CMDP. This methodology achieves superior asymptotic performance and enhanced learning efficiency. Experimental results across various CMDP tasks demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods that directly optimize CMDPs.

text: Many Siamese network-based trackers lack model update mechanisms, hindering their ability to adapt to target-specific variations. Furthermore, these trackers typically infer object states using axis-aligned bounding boxes, which can include background noise and fail to accurately estimate object rotation and scale, thereby potentially degrading tracking performance. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel Rotation-Scale Invariant Network (RSINet). The proposed RSINet comprises a target-distractor discrimination branch and a rotation-scale estimation branch, enabling explicit learning of rotation and scale knowledge through end-to-end multi-task learning. Additionally, the tracking model is adaptively optimized and updated via spatio-temporal energy control, enhancing model stability, reliability, and tracking efficiency. Extensive experiments on the OTB-100, VOT2018, and LaSOT benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed RSINet achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to recent trackers, operating at approximately 45 FPS.

text: This paper introduces the concept of a Doppelganger Graph, a novel graph structure that resembles a given original graph while maintaining distinct characteristics. The objective is to generate a synthetic graph that preserves key properties of the original, such as degree distribution and community structure, yet differs in significant ways. To achieve this, we propose a hybrid approach combining graph embedding techniques and generative models. Our method first learns a compact representation of the original graph using node embeddings, and then utilizes a generative adversarial network to produce a new graph that mimics the original's characteristics while introducing random perturbations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in generating Doppelganger Graphs that are both similar and distinct from the originals. The proposed method has significant implications for graph anonymization, data augmentation, and graph-based machine learning applications. Key contributions include a novel graph generation framework, improved preservation of graph properties, and enhanced control over the similarity and distinctness of the generated graphs. Relevant keywords: graph generation, graph embedding, generative models, graph anonymization, data augmentation.

text: This paper proposes AFEX (Attention-like Feature EXplanation), a novel system for local and global explanation of machine learning black-box model predictions by tabular data. AFEX identifies pairwise interactions between features based on shape function multiplications. A modification incorporating an additional surrogate model is also proposed. AFEX is trained end-to-end on a whole dataset only once, eliminating the need for retraining during the explanation stage. Numerical experiments with synthetic and real data illustrate the method's efficacy and contributions to interpretable machine learning.

text: This paper addresses the problem of low-rank matrix recovery, a fundamental challenge in machine learning and signal processing. Our objective is to develop an efficient algorithm that achieves fast global convergence for this task. We propose a Riemannian gradient descent method with random initialization, which leverages the geometric structure of the low-rank matrix manifold to escape local minima and converge to the global optimum. Our approach utilizes a carefully designed metric and retraction operation to ensure efficient optimization on the manifold. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing algorithms in terms of convergence speed and accuracy, even with random initialization. The key findings of this study include a provable global convergence guarantee and a significant reduction in computational complexity. Our research contributes to the development of efficient low-rank matrix recovery algorithms, with potential applications in image and signal processing, recommender systems, and machine learning. The novelty of our approach lies in its ability to combine the benefits of Riemannian optimization with the simplicity of random initialization, making it a promising tool for large-scale matrix recovery tasks. Key keywords: low-rank matrix recovery, Riemannian gradient descent, random initialization, global convergence, machine learning, signal processing.

text: Breast cancer screening remains a critical component of women’s health, yet current AI-embedded devices fall short of the accuracy desired by clinicians, prompting the need for more reliable intelligent systems. This paper addresses this challenge through a three-pronged approach: first, employing the SRGAN super-resolution network to enhance ultrasound image clarity and thus improve detection accuracy and model generalization; second, optimizing the YOLOv4 and CenterNet models to better meet the specific requirements of medical imaging; and third, implementing a multi-AI strategy that leverages cross-validation between two AI models, accepting only consistent results to increase reliability. Results show that integrating the super-resolution model increases the mAP score of YOLOv4 and CenterNet by 9.6% and 13.8%, respectively, and two novel methods for adapting detection models to classification tasks enable unified outputs for multi-model processing. In classification evaluations, while the YOLOv4 and CenterNet models achieved sensitivities of 57.73% and 62.64% and specificities of 90.08% and 92.54%, the multi-AI model, by declining to judge 23.55% of inputs, reached significantly higher sensitivity (95.91%) and specificity (96.02%). These findings demonstrate that the proposed methodology enhances AI reliability in medical image diagnosis, suggesting a promising direction for future research in adapting target detection models from diverse fields to medical lesion screening and improving diagnostic trustworthiness.

text: Estimating lighting from a single image is a crucial yet demanding challenge in the fields of computer vision and graphics. Traditional approaches attempt to determine lighting by either regressing key illumination parameters or creating illumination maps directly, but these techniques frequently lack precision and generalizability. This study introduces Geometric Mover's Light (GMLight), a framework for lighting estimation that integrates a regression network with a generative projector for precise illumination assessment. The framework models illumination scenes by considering geometric light distribution, light intensity, ambient term, and auxiliary depth, treating the estimation as a purely regression problem. Drawing inspiration from the earth mover's distance, we develop an innovative geometric mover's loss to accurately guide the regression of light distribution parameters. Utilizing the derived lighting parameters, the generative projector constructs panoramic illumination maps with realistic visual quality and frequency. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that GMLight provides precise illumination estimation and exceptional fidelity in relighting scenarios for 3D object insertion.

We posit that this formulation may yield stronger generalization capacity, in line with the outcomes of existing applications of AVI to deep networks. text: Decentralized Online Learning (DOL), which pertains to online learning within decentralized network architectures, is garnering increasing scholarly interest. This heightened focus stems from the premise that DOL facilitates data providers in cooperatively addressing their online optimization challenges more effectively, circumventing the need to disclose private data to external third parties or other network participants. Collaboration is typically established through the exchange of local models, such as recommendation models, among neighboring data providers. Nevertheless, the current optimal regret bound reported for decentralized online learning algorithms is \Ocal}, where n represents the number of nodes (or users) and T denotes the number of iterations. This outcome is notably suboptimal, as an equivalent bound can be attained without any inter-node communication. This observation prompts a fundamental inquiry regarding the conditions under which and reasons for which communication contributes to regret reduction in decentralized online learning. This paper investigates these aspects. Specifically, our analysis characterizes each loss function by two distinct components: an adversarial component and a stochastic component. Within this framework, we demonstrate that the Decentralized Online Gradient (DOG) algorithm achieves a regret bound of \OcalG + \sigma}, where G quantifies the magnitude of the adversarial element present in the private data (or the local loss function), and \sigma quantifies the inherent randomness within the private data. This derived regret bound implies that leveraging the stochasticity within private data through the exchange of information can yield performance benefits. A further significant contribution of this study involves the consideration of dynamic regret, a more practically relevant metric for tracking evolving user interests. Empirical investigations are additionally presented to corroborate our theoretical findings.

text: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) studies have grown exponentially in the past few years. Their impact has been seen mainly in the computer vision field with realistic image and video manipulation, especially generation, making significant advancements. While these computer vision advances have garnered much attention, GAN applications have diversified across disciplines such as time series and sequence generation. As a relatively new niche for GANs, fieldwork is ongoing to develop high quality, diverse and private time series data. In this paper, we review GAN variants designed for time series related applications. We propose a taxonomy of discrete-variant GANs and continuous-variant GANs, in which GANs deal with discrete time series and continuous time series data. Here we showcase the latest and most popular literature in this field; their architectures, results, and applications. We also provide a list of the most popular evaluation metrics and their suitability across applications. Also presented is a discussion of privacy measures for these GANs and further protections and directions for dealing with sensitive data. We aim to frame clearly and concisely the latest and state-of-the-art research in this area and their applications to real-world technologies.

text:
The rapid growth of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) has highlighted the need for portable, reusable, and reproducible workflows to streamline the deployment and benchmarking of machine learning models. This paper introduces *CodeReef*, an open platform designed to address these challenges by providing a unified environment for MLOps automation, reusable actions, and reproducible benchmarking. The platform leverages containerization and workflow orchestration to ensure portability across diverse computing environments, enabling seamless integration with existing MLOps pipelines. *CodeReef* incorporates a modular architecture that supports reusable automation actions, reducing redundancy and accelerating development cycles. Additionally, the platform introduces a novel benchmarking framework that ensures reproducibility by capturing all dependencies, configurations, and execution environments. Experimental results demonstrate *CodeReef*'s ability to achieve consistent performance across different hardware and software setups, outperforming traditional ad-hoc approaches in terms of efficiency and reliability. The platform’s contributions include enhanced portability, reduced development overhead, and improved reproducibility, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the MLOps ecosystem. *CodeReef* is open-source, fostering community-driven innovation and adoption in the field.  

**Keywords**: MLOps, reproducibility, benchmarking, automation, containerization, workflow orchestration, open-source platform.

Quyền hạn này là cần thiết để khắc phục các lỗi nhập liệu, bổ sung thông tin thiếu sót, hoặc điều chỉnh nội dung báo cáo để đảm bảo tuân thủ các tiêu chuẩn nghiệp vụ và quy định hiện hành trước khi báo cáo được phê duyệt chính thức và đưa vào sử dụng. Để đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn và khả năng truy vết của dữ liệu, mọi thao tác sửa đổi đều được ghi lại chi tiết trong nhật ký kiểm toán (audit log) của hệ thống, bao gồm ID người dùng thực hiện, dấu thời gian, và các trường dữ liệu cụ thể đã được thay đổi. Hơn nữa, hệ thống được thiết kế để hỗ trợ kiểm soát phiên bản (version control), cho phép lưu trữ lịch sử các lần sửa đổi và khả năng hoàn nguyên về các phiên bản trước đó nếu cần thiết. Sau khi sửa đổi, báo cáo sẽ tự động được chuyển về trạng thái "Đã sửa đổi, chờ duyệt" (Modified, Pending Approval), yêu cầu một quy trình phê duyệt lại từ cấp quản lý cao hơn để xác nhận tính chính xác và hợp lệ của dữ liệu đã được chỉnh sửa. Quyền truy cập và thực hiện chức năng sửa đổi này được kiểm soát chặt chẽ thông qua các cơ chế xác thực và phân quyền (Authentication and Authorization) dựa trên vai trò người dùng (Role-Based Access Control - RBAC) nhằm ngăn chặn truy cập trái phép và đảm bảo an toàn thông tin.

text: Đặt vấn đề: Diclofenac là một loại hoạt chất thường dùng trong điều trị giảm đau, kháng viêm thường được bào chế dưới dạng viên nén giải phóng nhanh có tác dụng tức thời nhưng không kéo dài hoặc viên phóng thích kéo dài nhưng khởi phát tác dụng chậm. Nghiên cứu bào chế viên nén hai lớp diclofenac natri phóng thích có kiểm soát nhằm kết hợp được ưu điểm của hai dạng bào chế trên và tăng sự tuân thủ khi sử dụng thuốc. Đối tượng và phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu đã đánh giá công thức bào chế và các thông số xử lý quan trọng trong quá trình bào chế viên nén hai lớp sử dụng kỹ thuật tạo hạt ướt và dập trực tiếp. Lớp diclofenac natri giải phóng kéo dài được bào chế bằng cách sử dụng tá dược hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) có độ nhớt khác nhau (bao gồm 4000cps, 100000cps và 200000cps,..). Nghiên cứu giải phóng thuốc in vitro được đánh giá bằng cách tiến hành thử nghiệm độ hòa tan trong 10 giờ. Kết quả: Công thức và quy trình bào chế đã được thiết lập để thu được viên nén hai lớp chứa diclofenac natri 100 mg với một lớp giải phóng nhanh và một lớp giải phóng kéo dài. Đồ thị độ hòa tan của viên nén diclofenac natri cho thấy 55,52 ± 3,95% lượng hoạt chất trong lớp phóng thích tức thời được giải phóng hoàn toàn trong 45 phút đầu tiên và lượng hoạt chất còn lại được giải phóng kéo dài trong 10 giờ sau đó. Kết luận: Viên nén hai lớp chứa diclofenac natri 100 mg đã được bào chế thành công với đặc tính giải phóng hai pha như mong muốn. Trong tương lai viên nén hai lớp sẽ tiếp tục để thử nghiệm nghiên cứu trên in vivo . Công thức tối ưu trong nghiên cứu sẽ được thử nghiệm về dược động học in vivo trên chó.

text: Để đảm bảo tính tương thích và hiệu quả vận hành khi tích hợp với các nền tảng cửa hàng trực tuyến, một yêu cầu tiên quyết là khách hàng cần phải sở hữu tài khoản đã đăng ký trên hệ thống của cửa hàng. Cơ chế này không chỉ phục vụ cho việc quản lý định danh người dùng mà còn là nền tảng cho các tính năng cá nhân hóa và theo dõi đơn hàng, một khía cạnh đã được nhiều tác giả nhấn mạnh (ví dụ, Smith, 2021; Nguyen, 2022 về tầm quan trọng của trải nghiệm người dùng). Trong khi các công trình trước đây thường tập trung vào việc tối ưu hóa quy trình đăng ký nhằm giảm thiểu rào cản cho người dùng (Jones et al., 2020) hoặc tăng cường các biện pháp bảo mật tài khoản trong môi trường thương mại điện tử (Brown, 2019), nghiên cứu hiện tại đóng góp vào lĩnh vực này bằng cách khảo sát và đề xuất một mô hình tích hợp, trong đó việc tạo và sử dụng tài khoản được đồng bộ hóa chặt chẽ với kiến trúc hệ thống, từ đó nâng cao hiệu quả quản lý và trải nghiệm người dùng tổng thể.

text: Feature Pyramid Network (FPN)-based detectors have achieved significant progress in general object detection tasks, as evidenced by their performance on datasets such as MS COCO and PASCAL VOC. However, these detectors exhibit limitations in specific scenarios, particularly tiny object detection. This paper argues that the top-down connections between adjacent layers in FPNs exert both positive and negative influences on tiny object detection performance. To address this, we propose a novel concept, the "fusion factor," which enables control over the information flow from deep to shallow layers, thereby adapting FPNs for tiny object detection. Through a series of experiments and analysis, we detail a statistical method for estimating an effective fusion factor value for a particular dataset, with this estimation dependent on the distribution of objects within each layer. Comprehensive experiments conducted on tiny object detection datasets, including TinyPerson and Tiny CityPersons, demonstrate that configuring FPN with an appropriate fusion factor significantly enhances network performance over baseline models. Codes and models will be released.

text: Molecular optimization can be conceptualized as a graph-to-graph translation problem, wherein the objective is to transform a molecular graph into another with enhanced properties by leveraging a dataset of paired molecules. Given the multitude of ways in which molecules can be optimized, each input graph may correspond to several valid translations, presenting a challenge in modeling diverse outputs. This research introduces a junction tree encoder-decoder framework designed to facilitate diverse graph translations. Additionally, a novel adversarial training approach is employed to align molecular distributions, ensuring that the model can produce varied and realistic outputs. The diversity in the output distributions is achieved through the use of low-dimensional latent vectors that influence the translation process. The effectiveness of this model is demonstrated through its application to various molecular optimization tasks, where it consistently surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods. This advancement signifies a significant step forward in the field, offering a robust tool for molecular optimization that accommodates the inherent diversity in chemical transformations.

text: Partial multi-label learning (PML), which addresses the challenge of learning multi-label prediction models from instances with overly comprehensive noisy annotations, has recently attracted attention from the scholarly community. In this study, we introduce a novel adversarial learning model, PML-GAN, within a generalized encoder-decoder framework for partial multi-label learning. The PML-GAN model employs a disambiguation network to detect noisy labels and utilizes a multi-label prediction network to associate the training instances with the clarified label vectors, while implementing a generative adversarial network as a reverse mapping from label vectors to data samples in the input feature space. The learning process of the comprehensive model is represented as a minimax adversarial game, which improves the alignment of input features with output labels through a bi-directional mapping. Extensive experiments are conducted on multiple datasets, wherein the proposed model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance for partial multi-label learning.

text: Efficient exploration in online reinforcement learning (RL) is particularly challenging in high-dimensional environments with sparse rewards. While count-based upper confidence bound (UCB) exploration methods achieve minimax near-optimal rates in low-dimensional, tabular settings, it remains unclear how to efficiently implement UCB in realistic RL tasks with non-linear function approximation. To address this, we propose a new exploration method based on the deviation of the next policy's occupancy from previously explored regions, introducing this term as an adaptive regularizer to the standard RL objective to balance exploration and exploitation. We pair this objective with a provably convergent algorithm, yielding a new intrinsic reward that adjusts existing exploration bonuses. This intrinsic reward is straightforward to implement and can be combined with existing RL algorithms. In tabular settings, our method demonstrates improvements over count-only exploration strategies across various model-based and model-free algorithms. On navigation and locomotion tasks from the MiniGrid and DeepMind Control Suite benchmarks, our approach significantly improves sample efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. Code is available at https://github.com/tianjunz/MADE.

text: Most existing object detection methods rely on the availability of abundant labelled training samples per class and offline model training in a batch mode. These requirements substantially limit their scalability to open-ended accommodation of novel classes with limited labelled training data. We present a study aiming to go beyond these limitations by considering the Incremental Few-Shot Detection (iFSD) problem setting, where new classes must be registered incrementally (without revisiting base classes) and with few examples. To this end we propose OpeN-ended Centre nEt (ONCE), a detector designed for incrementally learning to detect novel class objects with few examples. This is achieved by an elegant adaptation of the CentreNet detector to the few-shot learning scenario, and meta-learning a class-specific code generator model for registering novel classes. ONCE fully respects the incremental learning paradigm, with novel class registration requiring only a single forward pass of few-shot training samples, and no access to base classes -- thus making it suitable for deployment on embedded devices. Extensive experiments conducted on both the standard object detection and fashion landmark detection tasks show the feasibility of iFSD for the first time, opening an interesting and very important line of research.

text: We present RON, an efficient and effective framework for generic object detection, motivated by smartly associating the strengths of region-based (e.g., Faster R-CNN) and region-free (e.g., SSD) methodologies. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC 2007, PASCAL VOC 2012, and MS COCO benchmarks demonstrate RON's competitive performance. Specifically, using VGG-16 and 384X384 input, RON achieves 81.3% mAP on PASCAL VOC 2007 and 80.7% mAP on PASCAL VOC 2012. Its superiority is more pronounced on larger and more difficult datasets like MS COCO, achieving 15 FPS with 1.5G GPU memory, making it 3X faster than Faster R-CNN. This work provides a promising direction for developing robust and efficient object detectors capable of handling diverse and complex real-world scenarios.

text: It is well established that training deep neural networks yields representations that capture essential features of the input data. However, the theoretical and practical understanding of these representations remains limited. In supervised learning, a key question is whether these representations encode features that are informative for classification while filtering out irrelevant or noisy information. We formalize this question by considering a generative process in which each class is associated with a high-dimensional manifold, with different classes corresponding to distinct manifolds. Within this framework, each input is generated using two latent vectors: (i) a "manifold identifier" \gamma, and (ii) a "transformation parameter" \theta, which moves examples along the surface of a given manifold. For example, \gamma may represent a canonical image of a dog, while \theta captures variations such as pose, background, or lighting. We provide both theoretical and empirical evidence that neural representations can be interpreted as LSH-like functions, mapping each input to an embedding determined solely by the informative \gamma and invariant to \theta, thereby effectively recovering the manifold identifier \gamma. A significant implication of this property is the potential for one-shot learning on previously unseen classes.

text: The effectiveness of deep learning, particularly in image classification applications such as automated melanoma detection, is significantly influenced by knowledge transfer. Deep learning models typically require extensive training data, which can be scarce in medical applications, making transfer learning—a technique that repurposes knowledge from models trained on other tasks—a valuable solution. While transfer learning is commonly used in state-of-the-art melanoma screening systems, a thorough assessment of its implementation has been lacking. This study examines the role of transfer learning, identifies optimal source tasks, and evaluates the benefits of fine-tuning (post-transfer model retraining). Additionally, we explore whether deeper, more computationally intensive models yield better performance. Our findings indicate that deeper models, pre-trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned, achieve superior results, with AUC scores of 80.7% and 84.5% on the two skin-lesion datasets tested.
